title: Opinion: Half of investment-grade bonds are only one step away from junk status
summary: This article discusses the precarious position of investment-grade bonds, noting that a significant portion is on the brink of becoming "junk" status. This situation arose as companies took advantage of cheap credit. The S&P 500 Index experienced a substantial decline in December, indicating potential market instability.

title: A.J. Gallagher’s 'clean coal' business draws ire of green investors
summary: Two prominent green investors, Green Century Funds and Calvert Funds, are re-evaluating their holdings in Arthur J. Gallagher & Co. following a Reuters investigation into the insurer's lucrative "clean coal" business. The investigation revealed that Gallagher's involvement in refined coal, despite government subsidies, has raised concerns about increased smog and elevated carcinogens in drinking water. This situation highlights the challenges in defining and vetting environmental credentials within the rapidly growing green investment sector.

title: Cramer Remix: 'It's too soon' to buy even this top-notch industrial stock
summary: Jim Cramer advises against buying Emerson Electric despite its quality, citing macroeconomic concerns like trade talks with China and oil prices. He also expressed frustration with hedge funds' influence on market swings based solely on oil prices and called for federal regulators to investigate rapid sell-offs like the one on Christmas Eve. Additionally, Cramer discussed backlash from his suggestion for Apple to acquire Epic Systems and gave his preferred fintech stocks: Mastercard, PayPal, and Visa.

title: A New Marriott Card Lineup Lets AmEx Launch a Contactless Expansion
summary: American Express is expanding its contactless card portfolio by leveraging its cobranded relationship with Marriott International. The new line of AmEx-Marriott "Bonvoy" cards will all feature contactless payment capabilities, building on AmEx's existing contactless offerings for Hilton and its Gold card portfolio. This move comes as other major issuers like JPMorgan Chase are also increasing their contactless card issuance in the U.S.

title: Kroger Plans to Widen It Ban on Visa Cards, Citing ‘Excessive’ Fees
summary: Kroger (KR) plans to expand its ban on Visa (V) credit cards to its Smith's Food and Drug division, citing "excessive" fees, particularly from premium cards. This move follows a similar ban implemented at its Foods Co. Supermarkets unit in California in July. Starting April 3, Smith's stores will no longer accept Visa credit cards, though Visa debit cards will still be permitted.

title: What Are Visa's Key Value Drivers?
summary: This article examines the primary value drivers for Visa (NYSE: V) stock, including its strong performance in recent quarters and key revenue streams. It details the contributions of data processing revenue, services revenue, and international transaction revenue to the company's valuation. The analysis also touches on the potential impact of market expansion into China and global digital payment trends.

title: The Story Behind the Real (And Fake) Names on Credit Cards
summary: This article delves into the origins of placeholder names seen on credit card marketing materials, revealing whether they belong to real people or fictional identities. It uncovers the stories behind names like CF Frost on American Express cards, D. Barrett on Chase cards, and Chris L Martin on Bank of America promotions. The piece explains why banks use these names to engage potential customers and reflects on the broader practice of displaying a name on a credit card.

title: Apple Card vs. American Express Platinum: A High-End Credit Card Face-Off
summary: This article compares the new Apple Card with the American Express Platinum, highlighting their features, fees, interest rates, and perks. While Apple aims to disrupt the credit card industry with its fee-free model and integrated ecosystem, American Express Platinum offers a suite of luxury benefits. The comparison aims to help consumers understand where Apple Card fits into the high-end credit card market.

title: Earnings preview: American Express (AXP) to cash in on cardmember spending, partnerships in Q1
summary: American Express (AXP) is expected to report diluted earnings of $1.98 per share on revenues of $10.45 billion for Q1 2019, driven by increased cardmember spending and strategic partnerships. The company has consistently topped earnings expectations, and analysts have a mixed "hold" and "buy" rating on the stock with an average price target of around $118.

title: A New Life For Visa API Portal, Visa Next
summary: Visa has re-branded its API portal as "Visa Next," adding new APIs and re-packaging services for issuing banks and partners to compete with Fintech payment platforms. Visa Next offers APIs for creating digital card accounts, instant activation, and tokenization for e-commerce and mobile wallets. Banks utilizing these APIs will need to address regulatory issues such as recipient screening, consent tracking, and KYC for various use cases like payments to 1099 workers.

title: fy19q2pressreleasefinal.htm
summary: Visa Inc. reported robust fiscal second quarter 2019 results with net income up 14% to $3.0 billion and diluted earnings per share up 17% to $1.31. Net revenues increased by 8% to $5.5 billion, driven by growth in payments volume, cross-border volume, and processed transactions. The company reaffirmed its full-year 2019 financial outlook while updating guidance for client incentives and effective tax rate.

title: Visa partners with PalmPay to drive financial inclusion across Africa
summary: Visa has partnered with PalmPay, a new Fintech player in Africa, to enhance financial inclusion across the continent through digital payment services. This collaboration will see PalmPay launch an app with a mobile wallet in Nigeria, Ghana, and Tanzania, offering various financial products and enabling both individual and merchant payments. The initiative aims to address the cash-centric nature of the region and provide access to digital payments for the unbanked.

title: American Express Enters The Reservation Game With Resy Acquisition
summary: American Express has acquired Resy, a reservation booking and management platform, to strengthen its presence in the highly competitive online reservation systems market. This move aims to make American Express more central to its customers' daily lives and retain card members by offering enhanced access to dining experiences. Resy, valued at $53 million USD and having previously acquired competitor Reserve, will continue to be led by its co-founders.

title: SWOT Analysis of American Express - AMEX SWOT Analysis
summary: This article provides a comprehensive SWOT analysis of American Express, detailing its strengths such as strong brand recognition and high market capital, and weaknesses like a declining traveler's cheque business and lack of debit cards. It also identifies opportunities for market expansion and increased product offerings, alongside threats from strong competitors and volatile economic conditions. The analysis highlights AMEX's position as a prestigious financial service provider and outlines potential areas for growth and concern.

title: Macro retoma su campaña para promover el uso de la tarjeta de débito entre sus clientes
summary: Banco Macro has relaunched its financial education campaign to encourage the use of debit cards by offering various prizes. For every 100 pesos spent with a Visa debit card, customers gets a chance to win a motorcycle or two 43-inch Smart TVs each month. The first drawing is scheduled for June 10, covering purchases made in May, with subsequent monthly drawings until December.

title: VGT ETF Down On Tech Stock Woes
summary: The Vanguard Information Technology ETF (VGT) experienced a downturn due to woes in the technology stock market, particularly with the Nasdaq being rattled. The article highlights Apple's decline due to regulatory concerns and mentions the broader risk associated with the concentration of VGT's portfolio in a few major tech companies. Analysts from D.A. Davidson noted increasing regulatory disruption potential for tech titans like Amazon, Apple, Facebook, and Google globally.

title: IEEFA report: GE made a massive bet on the future of natural gas and thermal coal, and lost
summary: A new IEEFA report reveals that General Electric (GE) and its major shareholders, including BlackRock, lost billions due to misjudging the global energy transition away from fossil fuels. GE lost investors an astounding US$193 billion in three years, representing 74% of its market capitalization, by failing to recognize the declining costs of renewables and increased energy efficiency. The report criticizes shareholders like BlackRock for not pushing back against GE's misguided strategy and urges divestment from fossil fuels into zero-emission industries.

title: Visa to acquire Rambus’ payments and ticketing business
summary: Visa announced its acquisition of Rambus’ payments and ticketing businesses to extend enhanced security benefits of tokenization beyond Visa cards to other transaction types, including domestic card networks and real-time payment systems. This move aims to facilitate safer, more secure payments across all forms of global commerce by combining Visa's network tokenization capabilities with Rambus' local and account tokenization technology. The acquisition will also bolster Visa's transit and mobility solutions offerings with Rambus' digital ticketing expertise.

title: CaixaBank, Global Payments and Ingenico Group partner to create an international innovation programme supporting startups in the fintech and business sectors
summary: CaixaBank, Global Payments, and Ingenico Group have partnered to create Zone2boost, an international innovation program supporting fintech and business startups. This initiative will identify, fund, and mentor innovative technology projects, aiming to promote the development of new products and services in the sector. The program, kicking off in Barcelona with a €5 million investment over three years, will provide startups with funding, co-working spaces, and advisory services.

title: PayPal Launches Instant Transfer in Canada Using Visa Direct
summary: PayPal Holdings Inc. has introduced Instant Transfer capabilities for individuals and small businesses in Canada, leveraging Visa Direct for real-time push-payments. This service allows users to move money from a PayPal account to a bank account via a Visa debit card for a 1% fee, up to $10. The expansion aims to provide quicker access to funds for Canadian users, following a similar launch in the U.S. earlier in the year.

title: Techron Advantage Cards from Chevron/Synchrony Get a Boost
summary: Chevron and Synchrony Financial have boosted their Techron Advantage Cards program. Customers can now earn up to 47¢ per gallon in Fuel Credits through various offers, including increased savings for premium fuel, new account bonuses, and Visa card purchases outside of fuel merchants, with the limited-time offer valid through December 31, 2019.

title: Sustainable Funds in the U.S. Saw Record Flows in the First Half of 2019
summary: U.S. sustainable funds achieved record-breaking net flows of an estimated $8.9 billion in the first half of 2019, surpassing the total for all of 2018. This trend is driven by an increase in available funds, more passive investment options, and major financial players entering the sustainable investing space. The strong inflows are expected to continue as investor interest grows and more funds establish solid track records.

title: Profile: Dennis Howard runs fast-growing Schwab tech hub in Austin
summary: Dennis Howard, CIO of Charles Schwab, leads the company's rapidly expanding tech hub in Austin. He oversees the technology operations for a company with approximately 20,000 employees and $3.5 trillion in client assets, having been influenced by his father's early advice about the future of computers. Before his role at Schwab, Howard was involved in IT at Visa and public policy in Washington D.C.

title: As auto talks open, a wide divide separates Detroit carmakers, UAW
summary: Negotiations between Ford Motor Co. and the United Auto Workers (UAW) have begun with a significant divide, as the UAW seeks job security and a share of record profits, while Ford aims to cut costs amid an industry shift towards autonomous and electric vehicles. UAW President Gary Jones emphasized that laborers deserve their due and warned against a "race to the bottom" despite corporate profits, while Ford leadership highlighted the need to remain competitive and address tough issues like health care costs and temporary employees. The article details the complex challenges facing both sides, including future technology investments, regulatory uncertainties, and the potential for strikes.

title: Best Visa credit card in India: Types, features and benefits
summary: This article provides a comprehensive guide to Visa credit cards in India, outlining different card types such as Classic, Gold, Platinum, Signature, and Infinite, along with their respective features and benefits. It also explains how to obtain a Visa credit card, how the Visa network operates, and essential tips for secure usage. Additionally, the article lists several Indian banks offering Visa credit cards and highlights options with no annual fee.

title: Travelers Companies Now Sends Insurance Claim Payments Via PayPal
summary: Travelers Companies, Inc. announced that its insurance customers can now receive claim payments via PayPal, allowing for faster reimbursement for auto, property, and general liability claims. This move aims to accelerate the recovery process for claimants, with plans to extend PayPal access to workers' compensation claimants in 2020. This initiative highlights a broader trend in the insurance industry towards adopting emerging technologies for more efficient and quicker disbursements, moving away from traditional slow-moving payment methods.

title: Inside the turnarounds at Western Union and MoneyGram
summary: This article examines the turnaround efforts at Western Union and MoneyGram, two major players in the cash payout space. It highlights Western Union's cost-cutting measures and strategic shifts towards digital and account-to-account payouts, while MoneyGram shows growth in digital transactions despite challenges in certain corridors. The article also provides a comparison of revenue per employee among major financial services companies, positioning Western Union towards the bottom and Visa as a leader.

title: Here are 2019’s biggest stock market winners and losers in the Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq
summary: This article reviews the biggest stock market winners and losers across the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq for 2019 up to August 29th. It highlights top performers like Chipotle, AMD, Apple, and Visa, and notes disappointing results for Macy’s and Kraft Heinz. Despite ongoing media narratives, the U.S. stock market has shown strong returns year-to-date, with the Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq Composite Index all posting significant gains.

title: IFA 2019: Presenting SoftPOS – A Solution that Turns Smartphones and Tablets into a Contactless Payment Terminal
summary: First Data (now Fiserv), Visa, and Samsung Electronics are showcasing their new SoftPOS solution at IFA 2019, which transforms smartphones and tablets into contactless payment terminals without additional equipment. This technology enables contactless transactions of any amount using embedded NFC functionality on mobile devices, accepting payments from cards, other NFC-enabled phones, or wearables. A pilot program for SoftPOS will launch in Poland by the end of 2019, with plans for expansion to EMEA and APAC regions.

title: Equinix Taps Uber Vet for CTO Slot
summary: Equinix has appointed Justin Dustzadeh, formerly Uber's head of global network and software platform, as its new Chief Technology Officer. Dustzadeh will be responsible for developing the company's technology roadmap, leading innovation, and contributing to its leadership in the cloud ecosystem. His extensive background includes roles at Visa, Huawei, Ericsson, and AT&T.

title: Wells Fargo appoints Charles Scharf as new CEO
summary: Wells Fargo has appointed Charles Scharf as its new CEO, making him the third chief executive in as many years, as the bank attempts to move past a series of scandals. Scharf will take over from C. Allen Parker on October 21st, after the bank has faced issues including millions of fake checking accounts and a $1 billion fine from federal regulators. Wall Street reacted positively to the news, with Wells Fargo shares rising almost 3%.

title: Wells Fargo Names Charles W. Scharf Chief Executive Officer and President
summary: Wells Fargo & Company announced the appointment of Charles W. Scharf as its new chief executive officer and president, effective October 21, 2019. Scharf, formerly CEO of Bank of New York Mellon and Visa Inc., will also join the Board of Directors. C. Allen Parker, the interim CEO, will support the transition and continue as general counsel.

title: Scandal-Plagued Wells Fargo Taps BNY Mellon’s Charles Scharf as New CEO
summary: Wells Fargo has named Charles Scharf, CEO of Bank of New York Mellon Corp., as its new chief executive officer, effective October 21. Scharf is tasked with turning around the bank after a series of scandals and improving its relationship with Washington regulators. He faces challenges including ongoing investigations, a growth restriction from the Federal Reserve, and declining revenue and loan balances.

title: Humana names Jennifer Bazante chief marketing officer - Bizwomen
summary: Humana Inc. has appointed Jennifer Bazante to the newly created role of chief marketing officer, where she will be responsible for strategies related to member acquisition, engagement, brand equity, and direct-to-consumer and business-to-business marketing. Bazante has been with Humana since 2014 and previously held the position of senior vice president of brand and acquisition marketing. This appointment follows another recent leadership change at Humana, with Karen Katz elected to the board of directors, indicating a focus on retail and customer experience.

title: 7 Things You Don’t Know About Wells Fargo’s New CEO
summary: This article introduces Charlie Scharf as the new CEO of Wells Fargo, highlighting his background working with Wall Street legends like Jamie Dimon and Sandy Weill, his previous leadership roles at Visa and BNY Mellon, and his family-first management philosophy that led him to resign from Visa. It delves into his management style, his belief in constant evolution, and his perspective on key issues facing the banking industry, such as digital transformation and branch networks. The article suggests that Scharf's experience and approach position him uniquely to lead Wells Fargo through its recovery from recent scandals.

title: Intuit QuickBooks and Visa Enable Real-Time Access to Funds Anytime, Anywhere for Small Businesses
summary: Intuit QuickBooks and Visa have partnered to introduce Instant Deposit, a new feature for QuickBooks Payments users that enables real-time access to funds. This initiative aims to address a major challenge for small businesses: cash flow, by allowing them to deposit payments directly to their eligible debit cards via Visa Direct 24/7. The service, which carries a 1% additional fee, is rolling out to U.S. customers and is expected to be generally available by the end of 2019.

title: Huntington Bancshares to cut 150 to 200 jobs in cost-cutting move
summary: Huntington Bancshares announced it will cut 150 to 200 jobs across its Midwest operations in response to a rapidly changing interest rate environment impacting revenue. The bank stated it needs to reduce expenses and adjust staffing levels, despite understanding the decision's weight on its employees. Separately, the company announced Zachary Wasserman will replace Mac McCullough as the new CFO, effective November 4th.

title: Huntington Bank taps veteran Visa executive as new CFO
summary: Huntington Bank has hired a veteran Visa executive as its new Chief Financial Officer. This appointment comes as the company is strategically strengthening its financial position in anticipation of a potential economic downturn. The article also provides related content about Huntington Bank's financial standing and growth strategies.

title: Huntington Announces Appointment of New Chief Financial Officer
summary: Huntington Bancshares, Inc. announced the appointment of Zachary J. Wasserman as its new senior executive vice president and chief financial officer, effective November 4, 2019. Wasserman, with previous experience at Visa, Inc. and American Express, will be responsible for finance, strategic planning, mergers and acquisitions, investor relations, treasury, tax, and accounting. He will succeed Howell D. "Mac" McCullough, who is retiring at the end of 2019.

title: Huntington Bancshares hires new CFO, will lay off up to 200 workers
summary: Huntington Bancshares announced it will cut 150 to 200 jobs due to volatile interest rates impacting revenue, while simultaneously appointing Zachary Wasserman as its new CFO, effective November 4. Current CFO Mac McCullough will stay on until December 31 for a smooth transition. The bank clarified there is no correlation between the new CFO hiring and the layoffs.

title: Visa, Mastercard and Amex Develop Remedy for Abandoned Online Purchases
summary: Visa, Mastercard, American Express, and Discover Financial Services have collaborated to create a one-click checkout option to combat online cart abandonment. This new "click to pay" button aims to simplify mobile purchases by eliminating the need to re-enter credit card details, competing with established services like PayPal and Apple Pay. Early adopters include Saks Fifth Avenue, Staples, and Papa John’s, with the card companies phasing out their previous individual checkout solutions.

title: Visa, Mastercard Say They Just Made Mobile Shopping a Lot Easier
summary: Visa, Mastercard, American Express, and Discover have partnered to launch a one-click checkout option for online mobile shopping, aiming to simplify the purchasing process and reduce "online cart abandonment." This new service competes with existing offerings from PayPal and Apple Pay by allowing consumers to save their payment details and bypass the need to manually enter credit card information for each transaction. The initiative seeks to address the frustration associated with inputting credit card details on small screens, which currently costs retailers billions in lost sales.

title: Cashless no more: Kroger Visa credit card ban ended following year-long fight over fees
summary: Kroger has ended its more than year-long ban on Visa credit cards, now accepting them at all of its stores nationwide. The supermarket giant had previously stopped accepting Visa at some subsidiaries due to "excessive fees," but has since reversed its decision. While the specific terms of the resolution are unknown, analysts view this as a win for Visa and the broader card industry, avoiding potential consumer-unfriendly surcharges or lost sales for merchants.

title: American Express Relaunched the Green Card—And It's Greener Than the Original
summary: American Express has relaunched its Green Card, now named Green from Amex, featuring a design primarily manufactured from plastic recovered from oceans and coasts in partnership with Parley for the Oceans. This initiative is part of Amex's broader commitment to eliminate single-use plastics and includes a card recycling program and options for customers to redeem reward points for eco-friendly products. Other financial institutions like Mastercard and Visa are also taking steps to reduce their environmental impact, reflecting a growing consumer demand for environmentally conscious companies.

title: Shaking the Latin American Equilibrium: The Petrobras & Odebrecht Corruption Scandals
summary: This article details the massive Petrobras and Odebrecht corruption scandals, which began as a small money laundering investigation in Brazil and uncovered widespread bribery and fraud across Latin America. It examines the profound impact of these scandals, including major settlements with U.S. authorities and the resulting push for political and corporate reform in the region. The author discusses how these events are challenging deeply entrenched institutional corruption, possibly leading to more transparent and competitive markets.

title: Visa moving global HQ, up to 1,500 employees to Giants' Mission Rock
summary: Visa announced its decision to move its global headquarters and up to 1,500 employees to the Giants' Mission Rock development in San Francisco. The company will occupy a 300,000-square-foot, 13-story office building, while maintaining its offices in Foster City. This move signifies a major corporate relocation to the new Mission Rock development.

title: Phil Heasley Announces Retirement From ACI Worldwide
summary: Phil Heasley, president of ACI Worldwide, a leading global payments player, announced his retirement after 15 years at the helm. His retirement comes as ACI Worldwide reports strong performance, with 3Q19 revenue growing 45% and anticipated full-year 2019 revenue between $1.315 billion and $1.345 billion. Heasley, who spent four decades in the payments industry, previously held executive positions at Paypower, First USA Bank, U.S. Bancorp, and Citicorp.

title: Phil Heasley retires from ACI Worldwide
summary: Phil Heasley has announced his retirement from ACI Worldwide after 15 years as president, CEO, and board member. The announcement comes at a time when ACI is performing strongly, following its entry into the industry in 1975. Heasley had a significant impact on the payments industry, previously holding executive roles at Paypower, First USA Bank, US Bancorp, and Citicorp.

title: Elavon to acquire Sage Pay, a gateway that competes with Stripe, PayPal and Adyen, for $300M
summary: Elavon, a subsidiary of US Bancorp, announced its acquisition of Sage Pay for £232 million ($300 million). This deal aims to boost Elavon's presence in the European e-commerce market, particularly in the UK and Ireland, and reflects the ongoing consolidation trend in the fragmented payment processing industry. Sage Group, Sage Pay's owner, is divesting payment assets to focus on accounting and payroll software.

title: American Express offers merchants up to $450K sign-on bonus to boost acceptance
summary: American Express is offering sign-on bonuses of $10,000 to $450,000 to encourage businesses to accept its payment cards, aiming to close the acceptance gap with Mastercard and Visa. This strategy is part of a multiyear effort to expand its merchant network and counter higher interchange fees, despite AmEx customers typically spending more. The company has focused on strategically targeting holdout merchants and salesforce incentives to achieve this growth.

title: PAGS Stock Price, Quote & Chart | PAGSEGURO DIGITAL LTD-CL A (NYSE:PAGS)
summary: This article provides a detailed overview of PagSeguro Digital Ltd. (NYSE: PAGS) stock, including its current price of $9.37, performance metrics, and key statistics. It also covers technical and fundamental analysis ratings from ChartMill, recent earnings reports, analyst forecasts, and company profile information. Investors can find data on market capitalization, P/E ratio, dividend yield, and future growth expectations for this financial technology company.

title: Visa and MoneyGram Partner on Debit Card Cross Border Transactions
summary: MoneyGram has partnered with Visa to enhance its debit card solution, allowing nearly instant cross-border fund transfers to select countries via Visa Direct. This expansion leverages Visa's real-time push payments platform for international P2P debit card deposit services, starting with the U.S. to Spain and the Philippines. The collaboration aims to capitalize on the growing demand for real-time P2P payments, especially through mobile transactions, and boost MoneyGram's digital business.

title: MoneyGram expands Visa Direct service to Spain, Philippines
summary: MoneyGram International Inc. has expanded its debit card deposit service to Spain and the Philippines through Visa Direct, a real-time push payments platform. This expansion builds on their initial launch last year and marks MoneyGram as the first company to enable cross-border transfers from the U.S. using Visa Direct, with further expansion planned. The service allows customers to send funds to eligible Visa-branded debit cards via the MoneyGram app or website.

title: Vanguard Information Technology ETF: Expensive, But Should Be Okay To Continue To Own
summary: The article analyzes the Vanguard Information Technology ETF (VGT), noting its portfolio of large-cap technology stocks with competitive positions. Despite its current premium valuation, the fund is deemed suitable for continued ownership due to the long-term growth outlook of its holdings and their "moaty" characteristics like recurring revenues and strong ecosystems.

title: Visa buys fintech startup Plaid for $5.3B
summary: Visa Inc. has announced a deal to acquire fintech startup Plaid Financial Inc. for $5.3 billion in an all-cash transaction. Plaid, founded in 2013, provides a financial application programming interface that connects various apps and services with traditional financial institutions. The acquisition is expected to expand Visa's addressable market and enhance payment capabilities for fintech developers, with Plaid continuing to operate as a separate business unit under Visa's ownership.

title: Top 10 Tech Acquisitions of 2019 | YearEnder | Toolbox
summary: The article reviews the top 10 tech acquisitions of 2019, totaling $100 billion, by major tech and financial giants like Apple, Nvidia, Salesforce, FIS Global, Mastercard, and PayPal. These acquisitions aimed to diversify product offerings, introduce new features, and expand market presence in areas such as fintech, security, software, and hardware. The article also discusses key lessons businesses can learn from these acquisition trends, highlighting the drive for digital transformation and customer-centricity.

title: Stock that rose 8,500% in Hong Kong resumes trading with HK$19b plunge
summary: China Ding Yi Feng Holdings plunged 68% upon resuming trading after a 10-month halt, wiping out HK$19 billion in market value. The suspension followed a 8,500% rally and suspected market manipulation, leading Hong Kong regulators to commence proceedings against individuals linked to the company. The stock had previously been included in major indexes and attracted funds like BlackRock and Vanguard.

title: American Express catches up to Visa, Mastercard in acceptance, it reports
summary: American Express announced it has achieved "virtual parity" in merchant acceptance with Visa and Mastercard by adding 1 million U.S. merchants last year. This achievement is attributed to programs like OptBlue, which enticed small businesses with lower costs, and sign-on bonuses. Despite lingering public perception of higher fees, the gap in interchange fees between AmEx and its competitors is narrowing.

title: Swiping their way higher: Visa, Mastercard could be the next $1 trillion companies
summary: Visa and Mastercard are rapidly increasing in market value, with stocks up roughly 50% in the past year, leading some to believe they could be the next $1 trillion companies by 2023. Their growth is driven by the global shift towards cashless financial transactions and online shopping, with both companies holding significant shares of the credit and debit card market. Despite potential risks from increased competition and regulation, both firms are actively seeking acquisitions to boost their financial technology integration.

title: Remitly Launches Passbook – Banking Designed for Immigrants
summary: Remitly has launched Passbook, a new banking solution specifically designed for immigrants in the U.S. Passbook offers an online, no-fee account that eliminates common barriers to financial services, such as the need for a social security number, and includes immigrant-friendly features like global usability and customizable Visa Debit Cards. The service aims to transform banking for the over 44 million first-generation adult immigrants in the U.S., building on Remitly's mission to support this community.

title: Payment Processing Solutions Market - A Multi-Billion Dollar Market Identifying Hidden Gems
summary: HTF Market Intelligence Consulting Pvt. Ltd. published a new research study on the Global Payment Processing Solutions Market. The report offers a detailed product outlook, elaborates on market reviews until 2025, and identifies key players such as Wirecard AG, Visa Inc., and PayPal Holdings, Inc. The study segments the market by type, application, and region, providing qualitative and quantitative data to help companies understand market dynamics and develop strategic recommendations.

title: Despegar.com launches co-branded credit card in Brazil in partnership with Santander and Visa to complement its loyalty program
summary: Despegar.com's Brazilian subsidiary, Decolar, has partnered with Visa and Banco Santander (Brasil) S.A. to launch a co-branded credit card in Brazil. This new "Passaporte Decolar" card enhances Despegar's loyalty program, allowing customers to redeem accumulated points for travel products and services and offering online approval before the first travel purchase. This initiative aims to deepen customer engagement and expand brand awareness by rewarding customer loyalty.

title: Intuit near deal to buy Credit Karma for $7B
summary: Intuit, the maker of TurboTax and QuickBooks, is reportedly nearing a deal to acquire personal-finance portal Credit Karma for approximately $7 billion in cash and stock. This acquisition would be Intuit's largest ever and signifies a strategic move to expand its presence in consumer finance. The deal would allow both companies to refine customer recommendations by leveraging a larger trove of financial data.

title: TurboTax maker Intuit is buying personal finance site Credit Karma
summary: Intuit Inc., the company behind TurboTax, announced its acquisition of personal finance website Credit Karma Inc. for approximately $7.1 billion in cash and stock. Credit Karma, known for offering free credit scores and other financial services to over 100 million users, recently launched a free tax-filing platform, directly competing with TurboTax. This acquisition is part of a larger trend of mergers and acquisitions in the fintech industry, as established companies look to acquire startups for growth.

title: Fintech company Intuit to buy Credit Karma for $7.1 billion
summary: Intuit, known for TurboTax and QuickBooks, announced its acquisition of Credit Karma for approximately $7.1 billion in cash and stock. This move expands Intuit's presence in consumer finance technology, aiming to create a personalized financial assistant platform. Credit Karma, which provides free credit score monitoring and recommends financial products, reported nearly $1 billion in unaudited revenue in 2019.

title: American Express, Dow Inc. share losses contribute to Dow's nearly 850-point fall
summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average is experiencing a significant decline, largely due to losses in American Express and Dow Inc. shares. American Express shares are down 5.6% and Dow Inc. shares are down 5.4%, contributing substantially to the index's nearly 850-point intraday fall. Other companies like Visa, UnitedHealth, and United Technologies are also adding to the market downturn.

title: Visa Plans to Offer Credit Cards in Sudan After U.S. Sanctions End
summary: Visa Inc. is collaborating with three Sudanese banks to introduce its payment products in Sudan. This move follows the lifting of U.S. sanctions and a change in leadership in the North African country, signifying a new entry for Western businesses into the Sudanese market. The effort aims to expand electronic banking services in Sudan.

title: Technology trumps consumer staples in the hunt for quality
summary: This article argues that the traditional strength of consumer staples has waned, while the technology sector now offers superior investment opportunities, particularly when viewed through a "franchise power/growth framework." It highlights the shift in leadership from consumer staples to IT, attributing technology's rise to strong business franchises, network effects, and a move towards subscription-based software models. The author also compares the portfolio weightings and performance of various quality investment funds, showing a trend towards higher tech exposure.

title: XP Inc. Reports 4Q19 and Fiscal Year 2019 Financial Results
summary: XP Inc. reported strong financial results for Q4 2019 and the full fiscal year 2019, driven by significant growth in Assets Under Custody and active clients, coupled with a successful IPO. The company achieved a 72% increase in Gross Revenue to R$5.5 billion and a 119% rise in Adjusted Net Income to R$1.1 billion for 2019. XP Inc. also highlighted its strategic partnership with Visa to enter the debit and credit card market in Brazil, aiming to offer a complete banking experience and further disrupt the financial sector.

title: Pesapal to become Visa Principal Member driving small business acquisition and issuing
summary: Visa Inc. has partnered with Pesapal to enable digital payments for consumers and businesses in Africa, especially focusing on small businesses. Pesapal, now a Visa Principal Member, will leverage Visa's capabilities to allow more small businesses to accept various Visa payments, while also enhancing contactless payment options for consumers through Pesapal Mobile. This collaboration aims to expand payment acceptance and drive financial inclusion across Africa.

title: A financial account optimized for commerce | Shopify Balance
summary: Shopify Balance is an all-in-one financial account designed for e-commerce businesses, offering features like fast payouts, APY rewards, and no monthly fees. It allows merchants to manage funds, earn rewards, and simplify finances directly within their Shopify admin. The service provides up to six free accounts, FDIC insurance eligibility, and a Visa® Commercial Credit card to help businesses track spending and optimize cash flow.

title: What Kind Of Shareholder Appears On The Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals, Inc.'s (NASDAQ:ARWR) Shareholder Register?
summary: This article analyzes the shareholder structure of Arrowhead Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ:ARWR), revealing that institutional investors hold a significant 66% stake, while the general public owns 31% and insiders hold shares worth US$100m. BlackRock, Inc. and The Vanguard Group, Inc. are identified as the two largest institutional shareholders. The article emphasizes the power wielded by institutional investors due to their collective ownership and notes the positive signal of insider ownership.

title: Trump Administration Will Not Renew Marriott OFAC License To Manage Hotels In Cuba
summary: The Trump Administration announced its decision not to renew Marriott International's OFAC license to manage hotels in Cuba, specifically the Four Points Sheraton in Havana, forcing Marriott to cease operations by August 31. This move is seen as a continuation of the administration's policy to reverse Obama-era initiatives with Cuba, viewing commercial activities as unduly benefiting the Cuban government. Marriott expressed disappointment but hopes to return if U.S. government policy changes.

title: Visa to establish office in BD
summary: Visa Inc. announced plans to establish a country liaison office in Dhaka, Bangladesh, by the end of 2020. This move aims to introduce new services, drive social impact programs, and contribute to Bangladesh's economic growth and digital payment ecosystem. Having operated in Bangladesh since 1988, Visa seeks to further leverage the rapid growth of digital payments in the country with a dedicated local team.

title: Visa On How To Make Plastic Cards Sustainable
summary: Visa has partnered with CPI Card Group to launch new "Earthwise High Content Cards" made from up to 98% upcycled plastic, aiming to reduce plastic waste. Douglas Sabo, Visa's global head of corporate responsibility and sustainability, highlighted that these cards are made from post-industrial rPETG plastic, are EMV compliant, and support contactless payments. The initiative responds to consumer demand for environmentally conscious financial institutions, with CPI's survey showing 73% of respondents want their FIs to be eco-conscious.

title: Verizon, Synchrony launching consumer credit card
summary: Verizon is launching a consumer credit card in partnership with Synchrony, offering rewards on various purchases, particularly groceries and fuel, and on Verizon services. The card is exclusively for existing Verizon wireless customers, with rewards paid in Verizon Dollars redeemable for Verizon purchases. This move reflects a response to consumer trends influenced by the coronavirus pandemic.

title: Why Digital Turbine (APPS) Stock is a Compelling Investment Case
summary: This article highlights Digital Turbine Inc. (APPS) as a compelling investment, based on Greenhaven Road Capital's bullish thesis. The firm, which pitched APPS in February 2020, noted the company's strong revenue growth in both U.S. and international markets through partnerships with major carriers and app companies. The article also points out increased bullish hedge fund positions and Digital Turbine's significant stock performance since Greenhaven Road Capital's initial recommendation.

title: Canada is now the only Five Eyes member to not ban or restrict use of Huawei 5G equipment
summary: Canada remains the sole member of the Five Eyes intelligence alliance that has not banned or restricted Huawei's 5G equipment, following Britain's recent decision to prohibit new Huawei gear and remove existing components by 2027. This move has amplified pressure on the Canadian government from opposition parties and allies, including the U.S., who view Huawei as a security risk due to its ties with the Chinese government. Despite this, a decision from Ottawa is not expected soon, with cabinet having only discussed the issue once, although options like an outright ban or conditional inclusion are being considered.

title: Student loans center of 401(k) perk for Allianz workers
summary: Allianz Life has introduced a new benefit allowing employee student loan repayments to count towards their 401(k) employer match. This initiative, following a precedent set by Abbott Laboratories, helps employees overcome the challenge of saving for retirement while managing student debt. Allianz will consider loan payments as contributions to reach the full 7.5% company 401(k) match, even if employees don't make personal 401(k) contributions.

title: JPMorgan Chase partners with fintech start-up Marqeta to launch 'virtual' credit cards
summary: JPMorgan Chase is partnering with fintech start-up Marqeta to offer "virtual" credit cards for its commercial cardholders, allowing immediate use in mobile wallets. This eliminates the need for physical plastic cards and helps address needs intensified by the pandemic, such as remote work and contactless payments. Marqeta, which provides similar technology to DoorDash and Instacart, offers speed and modern technology that would take established financial institutions years to develop in-house.

title: Visa beats estimates as quarterly profit falls 23%
summary: Visa Inc. reported a 23% drop in quarterly profit, beating analysts' estimates despite consumer spending pressure from high unemployment due to coronavirus lockdowns. Net income fell to $2.37 billion, or $1.07 per Class A share, reflecting a 10% decrease in total payments volume and a 37% drop in cross-border volume. This marks the first year-over-year decline in quarterly revenue and adjusted net income since Visa went public in 2008.

title: In the search for a new king of credit cards, some surprise names emerge
summary: The credit card market is dynamic, with rewards constantly changing, making the search for a "king of credit cards" an ongoing process. Non-bank providers like Rogers World Elite Mastercard and Brim Financial have emerged as strong contenders, offering competitive rewards and no foreign transaction fees, challenging traditional bank offerings. Consumers are advised to look beyond their primary banks and compare features to find cards that best suit their spending habits and reward preferences, as even top-tier cards can be devalued over time.

title: Sprint stores get rebrand, begin operating under T-Mobile brand
summary: Sprint retail stores nationwide are officially beginning to operate under the T-Mobile brand following the $26 billion merger completed in April. The majority of Sprint stores have been updated with T-Mobile branding and can now serve both Sprint and T-Mobile customers, aiming to deliver a superior 5G network and enhance competition. T-Mobile also announced a new "Scam Shield" initiative to protect customers from robocalls and expects significant new postpaid subscriptions despite additional merger and pandemic-related costs.

title: BBVA te invita al Cosquín Rock Festival Online este fin de semana
summary: BBVA is inviting customers to the Cosquín Rock Festival Online this weekend, which will be a two-day interactive and immersive digital event featuring over 50 artists from across Hispanoamerica. BBVA customers in Argentina can purchase tickets with Visa and Mastercard credit cards in three interest-free installments. The festival promises a unique online experience including chat functions, meet & greets, and VR experiences.

title: American Express Said to Be in Talks to Buy Kabbage for $850 Million
summary: American Express is reportedly in advanced talks to acquire online lender Kabbage for an all-cash deal worth up to $850 million. This potential acquisition would further solidify American Express's presence in the small-business market, a sector from which 30% of its revenue is derived. The move follows similar high-value fintech acquisitions by Mastercard and Visa, indicating a broader trend among traditional card networks to integrate fintech innovation.

title: American Express makes Kabbage acquisition official
summary: American Express has officially acquired Kabbage's team, fintech products, data platform, and intellectual property for small businesses. The deal significantly enhances AmEx's reach into the small business market, which accounts for about 30% of its revenue, and comes after Kabbage played a major role in the Paycheck Protection Program. This acquisition is part of a larger trend of credit-card networks bolstering their technology assets through fintech acquisitions.

title: BMW, MINI and BMW Motorrad Enthusiasts Have a New Way to Display Their Brand Affinity, Earn Rewards with New Credit Cards from U.S. Bank.
summary: BMW Group Financial Services and U.S. Bank have launched a new suite of Mastercard credit cards for BMW, MINI, and BMW Motorrad enthusiasts. These cards offer accelerated rewards on purchases, including up to 5x at dealerships, and provide convenient features like contactless payments and a digital application process with instant approval for immediate use. The initiative aims to enhance customer loyalty and provide greater value and functionality to brand enthusiasts.

title: Bring Colour Back to the South East Asian Payments Landscape
summary: Southeast Asia is a key region for innovation and growth in real-time payments, with its internet economy projected to triple by 2025. A new paper highlights real-time payments, ISO 20022, and QR codes as critical enablers for the region's economic recovery and integration. Countries like Singapore, Thailand, and Malaysia are leading the way in payments modernization and digital overlay services, with efforts underway for greater cross-border interoperability.

title: BDO Network Bank ATMs now accept Visa, KFTC international cards
summary: BDO Network Bank announced that its ATMs now accept Visa and KFTC International cards, expanding cash access for cardholders with internationally-issued cards across its 250+ ATMs nationwide. This development aims to benefit foreign visitors, especially Korean nationals, given their significant presence in the Philippines as tourists and migrants. The bank plans to double its branches in the next four years to further reach unserved and underserved markets.

title: PNC Treasury Management Launches Business-to-Consumer Payment Capability
summary: PNC Treasury Management has expanded its payment offerings by adding push-to-debit card capabilities called Direct to Debit Card, developed in collaboration with Visa. This new solution allows businesses to send payments to consumers 24/7 through an eligible debit card, enhancing convenience and immediacy for various business needs such as payroll and independent contractor payments. PNC continues to invest in innovative payment solutions to transform the industry.

title: Amid Covid’s Impact, Installment Pay Gets a Lift With New Offerings From Mastercard And Sezzle
summary: Mastercard and online installment startup Sezzle are expanding their installment payment offerings, capitalizing on increased consumer demand due to Covid-19's impact. Mastercard is integrating with TSYS and other technology providers to allow cardholders to elect installment payments before, during, or after a purchase. Sezzle is launching a virtual card compatible with Google Pay and Apple Pay, enabling its buy-now-pay-later service for in-store purchases for the first time.

title: Axis Global Equity Alpha Fund of Fund Review: Should You Invest?
summary: This article reviews the Axis Global Equity Alpha Fund of Fund, which invests in Schroder International Selection Fund Global Equity Alpha. The author discusses the underlying fund's performance against its benchmark, highlighting a poor track record and high expense ratios, especially for the regular plan. The article concludes by recommending investors consider alternatives with lower expenses, such as the Motilal Oswal S&P 500 Index Fund, for international diversification.

title: Deal Closed | British Columbia Investment Management Corporation | Acquisition of 100 per cent stake in Tower Infrastructure Trust
summary: British Columbia Investment Management Corporation (BCI), in partnership with Brookfield Infrastructure Partners L.P. and other investors, has finalized the acquisition of a 100% stake in Tower Infrastructure Trust from the Reliance Group. This InvIT holds all shares in Reliance Jio Infratel Private Limited (RJIPL), which manages approximately 135,000 communications towers. The total equity commitment for this transaction, aimed at expanding Jio's telecommunication network to about 175,000 towers, was approximately USD 3.4 billion.

title: CMO Of The Week: Intuit’s Lara Hood Balazs
summary: This article features Lara Hood Balazs, CMO and General Manager – Strategic Partner Group at Intuit, highlighting how her team rapidly adapted marketing strategies during the COVID-19 pandemic, particularly after the tax deadline extension. Balazs discusses Intuit's initiatives like the QuickBooks PPP program and their support for the Black and LGBTQ+ communities. She also elaborates on the company's shift from live events to virtual platforms and her philosophy of customer-centric marketing.

title: The digital transformation: speed and convenience drive B2C payments
summary: Digital transformation is rapidly changing B2C payments, driven by customer demand for speed and convenience, especially among Millennials. The article highlights how technological advancements, particularly mobile technology and payment networks, are enabling businesses to digitize low-value consumer payments like refunds and rebates, significantly reducing costs and enhancing customer satisfaction. This shift leverages network effects, contextual remittance, and enhanced security measures to create a strong value proposition for both payers and customers.

title: Market value of big fintech companies rises to $1 trillion, more than the largest banks
summary: The market capitalization of major fintech companies like Visa, MasterCard, Square, and PayPal has surpassed $1 trillion, exceeding the value of the six largest U.S. banks. This shift reflects investors' favor towards software-based tech companies during the pandemic and fintech's increasing push into traditional banking services. Meanwhile, traditional banks face pressure from low interest rates and potential loan defaults.

title: 10 monopolies and why they make good investments
summary: This article explores the investment potential of monopolies and oligopolies, guided by insights from Peter Thiel and Warren Buffett on competitive advantage. It identifies ten companies with strong monopolistic or oligopolistic market positions, such as Amazon, Google, Facebook, Visa, and Airbus, highlighting their market shares and business models. The author also discusses the transient nature of monopolies, using examples like Kodak and Nokia, and suggests investing in a "moat" ETF for diversified exposure to such companies.

title: Wells Fargo CEO Scharf comes under fire over diversity comments
summary: Wells Fargo CEO Charlie Scharf faced significant backlash for comments made in June regarding the limited pool of Black talent for senior roles, despite the bank's pledge to double Black leadership and tie diversity efforts to executive compensation. Scharf later apologized, clarifying that his remarks were "insensitive" and stemmed from "unconscious bias." The controversy highlights broader issues of racial diversity in the financial industry, prompting other major banks and financial companies to announce their own diversity initiatives.

title: ETF of the Week: Renaissance IPO ETF (IPO)
summary: This article discusses the Renaissance IPO ETF (IPO), highlighting its strong performance in 2020 despite the pandemic and the resurgence of IPO activity. It explains how the ETF invests in newly public U.S. companies and diversifies core equity portfolios by offering exposure to unseasoned firms. The success of Snowflake's IPO is used as a recent example of the market's strength.

title: PayPal Adds QR Codes to a Visa-Branded Venmo Card Issued by Synchrony With an NFC Chip
summary: PayPal has launched a new Visa-branded credit card for its Venmo peer-to-peer payment service, featuring both a QR code for P2P transfers and an NFC chip for merchant acceptance. Issued by Synchrony Financial, the card aims to boost Venmo's revenue and offers personalized cash back rewards. This innovative card combines dual contactless technologies to position PayPal strongly in both physical and digital transactions, particularly as consumers increasingly opt for contactless payments.

title: Press Release: Introducing the Venmo Credit Card - Oct 5, 2020
summary: Venmo has introduced its first-ever Venmo Credit Card, issued by Synchrony and powered by Visa. This mobile-first credit card offers automatic cash back on every eligible purchase, dynamically personalizing rewards based on spending habits, and allows users to manage all card activities directly within the Venmo app. Key features include up to 3% cash back on top spending categories, custom card designs with QR codes, and virtual card access for secure online shopping.

title: BBVA launches Aqua, the first card without numbers or a CVV
summary: BBVA has launched Aqua, a new line of credit cards in Spain that enhances security by featuring a dynamic CVV code and omitting printed card numbers or expiration dates. This innovation aims to prevent fraudulent use both online and physically. The associated BBVA app also provides renewed payment management, allowing customers to easily access card details and control expenses, with plans for a global rollout of this experience.

title: TD Bank files lawsuit against Plaid, accusing it of trademark infringement
summary: TD Bank Group's U.S. subsidiary has filed a lawsuit against Plaid Technologies Inc., accusing the data aggregator of trademark infringement. TD Bank claims Plaid unlawfully uses its logo and green color scheme to deceive customers into providing personal financial data, which Plaid then stores, mines, and sells to third parties. The bank is seeking a court order for Plaid to cease and desist its unauthorized use of TD's intellectual property.

title: Conduent Transportation Receives 'Visa Ready for Transit' Certification for its ATLAS® Ops Fare Collection System to Boost Contactless Payments for Mass Transit Systems Globally
summary: Conduent Transportation's ATLAS® Ops fare collection system has received Visa Ready for Transit certification, promoting the use of contactless payments in mass transit globally. This certification validates the system's ability to offer secure and streamlined fare collection methods, including contactless cards and digital wallets. The move helps transit agencies meet the increased demand for touchless solutions, addressing concerns highlighted by the COVID-19 pandemic and improving the overall rider experience.

title: An Option for Every Customer: Regions Bank Partners with Visa® to Curate Four Distinct Credit Card Offerings
summary: Regions Bank has partnered with Visa to offer four distinct credit card options designed to meet the varying financial needs of its customers, ranging from rewards cards for those with excellent credit to secured options for building credit. The bank's "Regions 360" strategy focuses on a holistic view of customer financial needs, offering products tailored to different life stages and credit profiles. These offerings include cards with intro APRs, rewards points, and an innovative mobile app feature called LockIt for enhanced security.

title: MoneyGram and PayMaya introduce real-time payment solution for fund transfer from United States to the Philippines using Visa Direct
summary: MoneyGram and PayMaya Philippines have partnered to launch a new digital service enabling real-time money transfers from the United States to the Philippines via Visa Direct. U.S. customers can use the MoneyGram app or website to send funds instantly to any PayMaya Visa cardholder in the Philippines, facilitating quicker and more convenient remittances. This collaboration aims to enhance the customer experience and drive digital growth in one of the largest remittance markets globally.

title: PayPal launches crypto payment platform
summary: PayPal is launching a new service allowing U.S. customers to buy, sell, and hold various cryptocurrencies, and eventually use them to pay at 26 million merchants. This move is expected to significantly increase the mainstream acceptance of digital currencies, with PayPal managing price volatility risks for merchants by converting crypto to fiat for transactions. The service will initially include Bitcoin, Ethereum, Bitcoin Cash, and Litecoin, and will expand to Venmo and international markets.

title: Urban One Expands Into Financial Industry With One VIP Prepaid Debit Card.
summary: Urban One has launched One VIP, a prepaid Visa debit card designed for Black consumers, featuring a rewards program and a "Buy Black" initiative. This financial solution aims to provide access and empowerment while circulating Black dollars within the community, with a portion of rewards supporting charities focusing on people of color. The company sees this as a significant step to financially include and empower the Black community through tailored financial products.

title: Amazon Pay ICICI Bank credit card is fastest to cross 1 million milestone
summary: The Amazon Pay ICICI Bank co-branded credit card has rapidly surpassed 1 million cards issued in less than 20 months, becoming the fastest in India to reach this milestone. This success is attributed to its unique benefits such as unlimited rewards, instant issuance, direct crediting of points to Amazon Pay balance, and the introduction of a Video KYC facility. The card is now available to any registered Amazon India customer, including non-ICICI Bank clients, and offers various rewards and no-fee spending options.

title: The Truth About Prepaid Cards
summary: This article examines prepaid cards, distinguishing common misconceptions from their actual utility. It explains that while these cards do not build credit, they can be a financially sensible option for managing expenses or providing temporary financial stability, especially for the underbanked. The piece emphasizes evaluating costs, understanding fine print, and considering prepaid cards as part of a broader financial strategy.

title: Apple loses $450b in value on iPhone woes
summary: Apple Inc. has lost $450 billion in market value since its peak last month, with a recent 5.6% drop wiping out over $120 billion. The decline follows disappointing iPhone sales that missed analysts' estimates and a lack of holiday quarter guidance. This slump, along with other tech giants' performance, is raising concerns about future growth in the sector.

title: BMO and Visa Canada Collaborate to Introduce Two New Reward Credit Cards to meet Canadians Lifestyle Needs
summary: BMO Bank of Montreal and Visa Canada have partnered to launch two new reward credit cards, the BMO eclipse Visa Infinite and BMO eclipse Visa Infinite Privilege, designed to cater to Canadians' evolving lifestyle needs. These cards offer accelerated rewards earning potential, with up to 5x points on everyday purchases, tailored to daily spending habits, leveraging Visa's extensive payment network and benefits. The collaboration aims to provide greater flexibility and immediate, relevant rewards to cardholders, aligning with changes in consumer spending patterns observed during the early stages of post-pandemic recovery.

title: JPMorgan Chase’s QuickAccept first step to building SMB ecosystem
summary: JPMorgan Chase's QuickAccept payment acceptance solution, built on WePay technology, is the first step in the bank's vision to create a comprehensive ecosystem for small- to medium-sized businesses (SMBs). The solution offers SMBs real-time, fee-free access to funds accepted at the point of sale, a key differentiator in a competitive market. JPMorgan Chase aims to integrate payment acceptance with other financial services, leveraging its banking infrastructure to provide a one-stop-shop for diverse SMB needs.

title: Visa's Pursuit of Plaid Looks Too Much Like Facebook-Instagram
summary: The Department of Justice filed a lawsuit to block Visa's $5.3 billion acquisition of Plaid, arguing it eliminates a competitive threat in the payments market. Regulators are learning from past mistakes with Big Tech, such as Facebook's acquisition of Instagram, and are now taking a longer-term view on potential market impact. The article suggests Visa's attempt to acquire Plaid mirrors Facebook's acquisition of Instagram, highlighting how an established giant aims to absorb an emerging competitor.

title: Van Eck targets China’s retail fund market
summary: Van Eck has submitted an application to the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) to establish a public mutual fund company in mainland China, aiming to tap into the RMB 17.8trn retail mutual fund market. The firm plans to offer ETF products, including thematic ETFs, and multi-asset allocation solutions, leveraging its extensive experience in Chinese capital markets since 1992. Additionally, Van Eck intends to apply for a Qualified Domestic Limited Partnership (QDLP) license, allowing it to raise funds in China for offshore investments.

title: El Banco BBVA lanzó junto a Visa una billetera digital para hacer pagos con tecnología contactless
summary: BBVA Argentina, in collaboration with Visa, has officially launched a new NFC digital wallet, enabling customers to make contactless payments with their Visa debit or credit cards using their mobile phones. This is a first-of-its-kind development for Visa with an Argentine bank, making transactions quicker and more secure through tokenization. The system is currently available via the BBVA Go app for Android users and aims to capitalize on the 300% growth in digital wallet usage during the pandemic and the 75% of POS terminals in Argentina that support contactless payments.

title: HDFC Bank aims to grow merchant payments base to 20 million in 3 years
summary: HDFC Bank plans to expand its merchant network from 2 million to 20 million within the next three years. This expansion is supported by the upgraded Smart Hub platform, which offers various digital tools like a digital ledger, billing software, and inventory management. The bank intends to cross-sell loans and credit cards, including 'buy now, pay later' options, to further drive growth and deepen digital payment penetration across India.

title: Why Regulators Are Saying ‘Yes’ to Mastercard-Finicity But ‘No’ to Visa-Plaid
summary: Regulators have approved Mastercard's $825 million acquisition of data-networking company Finicity, while simultaneously suing to block Visa's $5.3 billion bid for its rival, Plaid. The disparity in regulatory action stems from the Department of Justice's concern that Visa's acquisition of Plaid would eliminate a potential competitor in the debit-networking sphere, thereby strengthening what it perceives as Visa's monopolistic position in that market. Conversely, the DoJ views Mastercard's acquisition as less likely to create such an anti-competitive environment, given Mastercard's different market position.

title: Looking Closer At T. Rowe Price's Dividend Growth ETF, 'TDVG'
summary: The T. Rowe Price Dividend Growth ETF (TDVG), launched in August 2020, is an actively managed ETF that seeks dividend income and long-term capital growth by investing in dividend-paying companies expected to increase their dividends over time. Managed by Tom Huber, this ETF typically holds 100-125 stocks like Microsoft, Apple, and Visa, focusing on business model durability and financial health with a "growth-at-a-discount" approach. It's designed for investors seeking a mix of income and capital appreciation from an experienced management team.

title: GM vs. Ford: What their EV split reveals
summary: General Motors and Ford are pursuing differing strategies for electrification, with GM aggressively investing in EVs and battery production, aiming to be a top seller, while Ford takes a more cautious approach, focusing on a few key models and buying batteries from suppliers. GM plans to invest $27 billion in EVs by 2025 and roll out 30 models, including significant battery advancements, whereas Ford will focus on making its EV endeavor profitable through services and targeted vehicle electrification. Experts believe GM's ambitious plans could significantly impact the U.S. auto industry and the global EV market.

title: HDFC bank services restored after hours of an outage affecting UPI and card payments
summary: HDFC Bank's services, including UPI, card payments, and ATM transactions, were restored on Sunday after an outage that began Saturday evening. Customers had reported issues with online banking, credit/debit cards, and linked third-party services. The bank acknowledged the outage was due to a data center issue and apologized for the inconvenience, though intermittent problems may still occur as systems stabilize.

title: Behind BNY Mellon’s war against B2B checks
summary: BNY Mellon is leading an effort to modernize B2B payments, moving away from labor-intensive and fraud-prone paper checks towards efficient digital solutions. They are utilizing tools like Bottomline Technologies' Paymode-X, The Clearing House’s Real-Time Payments (RTP) network, and Zelle to offer faster, more secure transactions with integrated data exchange. The bank's initiatives aim to mirror the ease of consumer payment experiences while providing the robust security and documentation features required by businesses, positioning them as an innovator in the rapidly evolving financial landscape.

title: Digital Currencies (XBT, EXT, XRP) Are Set to Go Mainstream Says PayPal CEO
summary: PayPal CEO Dan Schulman believes digital currencies are poised to go mainstream as more merchants adopt a "digital first" approach to payments. He noted that the shift towards smartphone payments, QR codes, and digital wallets creates a natural environment for digital currencies to flourish. This outlook was shared at the Web Summit conference, emphasizing the growing integration of digital payment solutions.

title: BBVA, first bank to issue recycled plastic cards in Argentina
summary: BBVA has become the first bank in Argentina to issue credit cards made from 85.5 percent recycled PVC plastic, demonstrating its commitment to sustainability and the fight against climate change. Initially available for Visa International and Visa Gold credit card renewals, this initiative will later expand to all BBVA credit and debit cards, featuring a "sustainability seal." This move responds to increasing environmental awareness among customers and aligns with Sustainable Development Goals.

title: Fidelity National Information Services Inc. stock rises Friday, outperforms market
summary: Shares of Fidelity National Information Services Inc. (FIS) rose 1.75% on Friday, closing at $149.86 and outperforming both the S&P 500 Index and the Dow Jones Industrial Average. This increase ended a two-day losing streak for the company's stock. Despite the rise, the stock remained $8.35 below its 52-week high.

title: BBVA con tarjetas de plástico reciclado
summary: BBVA in Argentina is launching recycled plastic cards, made from 85.5% PVC derived from plastic waste, becoming the first entity in the country to do so. These cards will initially be available for Visa International and Visa Gold credit card renewals starting April 2021, and will feature a "sustainability seal." This initiative is part of BBVA's broader commitment to sustainability, which also includes a digital tool for SMEs to calculate carbon footprints and efforts to reduce its own CO2 emissions.

title: Deal of the Year: American Express buys Kabbage
summary: American Express acquired Kabbage's team, fintech products, data platform, and internet protocol for small businesses in a deal estimated between $750 million and $1 billion. This acquisition highlights both companies' strategies to expand beyond their traditional services, with Kabbage moving beyond lending into checking accounts and AmEx aiming to strengthen its small-business offerings and become more essential to its customers. The move by American Express follows similar acquisitions by Visa and Mastercard, demonstrating a broader trend in the payments industry to integrate data aggregation and expand services.

title: Tipalti extends credit card capability through new partnership
summary: Tipalti has partnered with Plastiq to allow businesses to pay invoices using corporate credit cards, even if suppliers don't accept them directly. This collaboration aims to provide businesses with increased access to capital, card rewards, and improved short-term cash flow, automating accounts payable processes. While offering flexibility, the solution involves a fee from Plastiq, and companies must carefully weigh the benefits against potential costs and risks.

title: Cuando los datos de tu tarjeta acaban en manos de estafadores
summary: This article details a systematic scam affecting BBVA Perú clients, where personal and credit card data are compromised through telemarketing and courier services. Victims, often led to believe they are interacting with the bank, are tricked into returning their newly issued cards, which are then used by fraudsters to withdraw funds. The BBVA has acknowledged the scam but has not fully disclosed its investigation results or security measures, while affected clients are organizing to demand accountability.

title: As Digital Payments Heat Up, Fiserv Agrees to Acquire Card-Control Technology Provider Ondot
summary: Fiserv Inc. announced its agreement to acquire Ondot Systems Inc., a provider of card-control technology, for an undisclosed sum. The acquisition aims to enhance Fiserv's digital offerings by leveraging Ondot's platform to accelerate digital customer acquisition, improve card activation, and reduce service costs, thereby delivering a unified digital experience to clients. Ondot's technology allows cardholders greater control over their card usage, improves transaction recognition, and facilitates instant digital card issuance and activation.

title: The Intriguing Verizon Visa Credit Card
summary: This article reviews the Verizon Visa Credit Card, highlighting its benefits for Verizon Wireless customers. It details the card's features such as no annual fee, no foreign transaction fees, up to 4% back in Verizon Dollars on specific categories, and a sign-up bonus of $100 Verizon Dollars. The review emphasizes that while niche, the card offers substantial value through rewards and credits for those who are Verizon customers, making it a potentially lucrative option for managing Verizon-related expenses.

title: Why Wall Street Would Love to See a Merger of FIS and Global Payments
summary: Although merger talks between Global Payments (GPN) and Fidelity National Information Services (FIS) have reportedly ended, analysts remain bullish on both stocks, viewing the discussions as a positive indicator for valuations and future industry consolidation. Wall Street believes a merger would create significant synergies and cost savings, boosting FIS's revenue and earnings per share. The payment processing industry has seen considerable consolidation recently, and a combination of FIS and Global Payments would strengthen their market position.

title: The Soaring Stock Index You’ve Never Heard Of - WSJ
summary: The article discusses the S&P Completion Index, a lesser-known stock index that significantly outperformed the S&P 500 largely due to Tesla's presence. Tesla, which was the biggest stock in the Completion Index, has now moved to the S&P 500, impacting the performance of both indices and related ETFs. This shift has already led to a decline in Tesla's stock and changes in the performance of funds tracking these indices.

title: Alibaba,Tencent shares fall after reports of US investment ban
summary: Shares of Chinese tech giants Alibaba and Tencent dropped following reports that the Trump administration was considering banning U.S. investments in the companies. This potential move is seen as a significant escalation in U.S.-China tensions. The ban could impact capital markets, given the combined $1.3 trillion market value of Alibaba and Tencent.

title: Mastercard And Partners Will Test Common Android Phones And Tablets As Contactless POS Devices
summary: Mastercard is launching "Tap on Phone," a service that allows common Android smartphones and tablets to accept contactless payments without additional hardware. This initiative, developed by Mastercard Labs, aims to leverage the increasing adoption of contactless payments by consumers and merchants. Mastercard has partnered with NMI, Global Payments Inc., and CEG for distribution and initial testing, while adhering to PCI Security Standards.

title: Value vs. Growth: Widest Performance Gap on Record
summary: In 2020, large-growth funds significantly outperformed large-value funds, with an average return of 34.8% compared to value's performance. This 32 percentage point gap marked the widest performance difference on record, surpassing even the dot-com bubble year of 1999. The consistent underperformance of value strategies, especially amplified in 2020, has led to a substantial widening of longer-term return gaps across various market capitalizations.

title: Truist named official retail banking partner of National Football League
summary: Truist Financial has entered a multi-year sponsorship agreement to become the official retail banking partner of the National Football League (NFL), leveraging its existing partnership with Visa. This collaboration will grant Truist retail banking and marketing rights for NFL events and fan experiences, with a focus on community support through financial education and economic empowerment. The partnership launched with an ad campaign during the Super Wild Card weekend and will feature visible Truist branding during NFL programming.

title: Visa, Plaid call off $5.3 bln deal
summary: Visa and financial technology company Plaid have terminated their $5.3 billion merger agreement following a U.S. government antitrust lawsuit. The deal was originally proposed in January 2020 and was scrapped to avoid protracted litigation, despite Visa's confidence in prevailing in court. The U.S. Justice Department had argued that the acquisition would eliminate a competitive threat to Visa's alleged monopoly in online debit transactions.

title: Visa Elevates Top Lawyers as DOJ Scrutiny Scuttles Plaid Deal
summary: Visa Inc. promoted two top lawyers, Kelly Mahon Tullier and Julie Rottenberg, to new roles as the company prepared for a potential antitrust challenge from the Justice Department. This announcement came shortly before Visa terminated its $5.3 billion acquisition of Plaid Inc., which the DOJ had sued to block. Mahon Tullier was named executive vice president and chief legal and administration officer, highlighting a significant internal restructuring amidst the legal battle.

title: British Aircraft Company Cuts Supplies to Turkish Drone Manufacturer
summary: Andair, a British aircraft components company, has ceased supplying products to BAYKAR, a Turkish drone manufacturer, after an Armenian Embassy request and an internal investigation confirmed their parts were used in military drones during the Artsakh war. This follows similar actions by Canadian company WESCAM (due to government ban) and Austrian company Rotax, making Andair the third supplier to stop providing components to BAYKAR amid international pressure regarding Turkey's use of drones. American company Viasat also faced protests and indicated an intent to cut supplies to Turkey.

title: ICICI Bank ties up with Niyo to issue prepaid cards to MSMEs
summary: ICICI Bank has partnered with fintech Niyo to introduce the 'ICICI Bank Niyo Bharat Payroll Card' for workers of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). This prepaid card, powered by Visa, allows MSMEs to disburse salaries to their blue-collar workers up to ₹1 lakh, providing them with digital banking convenience and financial inclusion. The partnership aims to bring under-banked workers into the formal economy through a state-of-the-art salary disbursement solution that enables ATM withdrawals, online transactions, and PoS payments, supported by a multilingual mobile app and accidental death insurance.

title: ICICI Bank introduces prepaid cards for blue-collar workers with Niyo
summary: ICICI Bank has partnered with fintech company Niyo to launch prepaid cards for blue-collar workers in Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in India. These Visa-branded cards, known as the 'ICICI Bank Niyo Bharat Payroll Card', aim to bring under-banked workers into the formal banking ecosystem, offering convenience and digital banking safety.
