It highlights growing advisor interest in Ethereum as a legitimate asset class, the success of spot Bitcoin ETFs, and the preference among advisors for ETFs as a method to access the crypto market. The piece also details Ethereum's real-world utility and its role in decentralized applications, stablecoins, and DeFi.

title: Visa, Mastercard to pay $197 million to settle consumer ATM fee lawsuit
summary: Visa and Mastercard have agreed to a $197 million settlement in a class-action lawsuit filed by millions of consumers. The lawsuit accused the financial payment companies of colluding to keep ATM cash access fees artificially high. The settlement, which resolves claims from consumers who used bank-operated ATMs since 2007, is subject to court approval.

title: Visa, Mastercard Reach $198 Million Deal in ATM Antitrust Case
summary: Visa Inc. and Mastercard Inc. have agreed to a preliminary settlement of $197.5 million in an antitrust case, resolving allegations of fixing ATM fees. This agreement, which still requires court approval, concludes over a decade of litigation with ATM customers. It follows a prior $66.7 million settlement in 2021 with JPMorgan & Chase Co., Wells Fargo & Co., and Bank of America Corp. for similar claims.

title: Breakingviews - Capital One scales banking’s Mount Improbable
summary: Capital One's $35 billion bid for Discover aims to create the largest U.S. credit card issuer and a major payments network, but faces significant regulatory and competitive hurdles. CEO Richard Fairbank must convince regulators, merchants, and investors of the deal's value, as integrating Discover's payments network and achieving global acceptance will be a monumental task. The article highlights the low perceived value by investors and the challenges of international expansion in retail banking.

title: Coming of Age for Millennials: American Express Nails It Again
summary: American Express is successfully appealing to younger generations, specifically Gen Z and millennials, by offering premium credit cards with high annual fees that provide significant value to users. This strategic shift has led to substantial financial growth for the company, with stock prices rising and a projected 10%-plus annual revenue growth, and it is largely driven by their ability to book younger cardholders directly into their premium offerings. The company's focus on rewards, service, and cachet continues to foster strong customer loyalty across generations.

title: Adani One launches 2 credit cards in partnership with ICICI Bank
summary: Adani Group has entered the retail finance sector by launching two credit cards, "Signature" and "Platinum," through its consumer app Adani One, in partnership with ICICI Bank and Visa. These cards offer various benefits, including reward points on Adani One app services and complimentary perks at Adani airports. The initiative aims to integrate Adani's B2B businesses into the digital world and strengthen ICICI Bank's credit card portfolio, while Adani One continues to expand its service offerings and customer base.

title: eBay will no longer accept American Express, citing ‘unacceptably high fees'
summary: eBay has announced it will no longer accept American Express globally starting August 17, citing "unacceptably high fees" for processing credit card transactions. The online marketplace stated that customers have alternative payment options and that AmEx is no longer a necessary partner. American Express, in turn, claims eBay's cost to accept their cards is comparable to other networks and that their cardmembers typically spend more, finding eBay's decision inconsistent with increasing competition.

title: EBay to Stop Taking American Express After Fee Dispute
summary: EBay Inc. announced it will no longer accept American Express cards as a payment option starting August 17, citing "unacceptably high fees." American Express countered that its fees are comparable to other networks and believes eBay's decision is inconsistent with increasing competition. This move mirrors past disputes between major retailers like Amazon and Costco with credit card companies over transaction costs.

title: eBay to Discontinue Acceptance of American Express Payments Starting August 17, 2024
summary: eBay announced its decision to discontinue the acceptance of American Express payments globally starting August 17, 2024. This change is attributed to the "unacceptably high fees" charged by American Express, with eBay calling for more robust regulations to increase competition in the credit card network market. Customers will be notified to transition to alternative payment options available on the marketplace.

title: Affirm's New Deal With Alterra Mountain Company Boosts Travel Spending
summary: Affirm Holdings, Inc. announced an expanded partnership with Alterra Mountain Company, allowing travelers to use Affirm's "Buy Now, Pay Later" (BNPL) service for Ikon Passes, lodging, and lessons in the U.S. and Canada. This move aims to enhance customer flexibility and increase travel spending. Despite high interest rates, Affirm CEO Max Levchin stated the economy is resilient and consumers continue to use flexible payment options, contributing to the company's 95% stock gain over the past year.

title: How Is PayPal Holdings’ Stock Performance Compared to Other Fintech Stocks?
summary: PayPal Holdings, Inc. (PYPL) is a large-cap fintech company valued at $69.4 billion with over 426 million active accounts. Despite its market leadership and recent strong Q1 2025 earnings which beat analyst expectations, PYPL's stock performance has largely underperformed the Global X Fintech ETF (FINX) and rival Visa Inc. (V) over the past year. Analysts, however, remain optimistic with a "Moderate Buy" rating and a projected premium to its current market price.

title: EBay to drop American Express over fees, says customers have other options
summary: eBay announced its decision to stop accepting American Express globally starting August 17, citing "unacceptably high fees" for processing credit card transactions. The online marketplace stated that customers now have numerous alternative payment options available. American Express, in response, claims eBay's cost to accept AmEx cards is comparable to other networks and believes the decision is inconsistent with increasing competition.

title: Amex dismisses impact of eBay’s rejection
summary: EBay announced it will no longer accept American Express payments due to "unacceptably high fees," effective August 17th. American Express, however, downplayed the impact, stating that eBay accounts for less than 0.2% of its total network volume, but criticized eBay for limiting customer payment choices. The move highlights the ongoing tension between merchants and card networks over transaction fees.

title: eBay to End American Express Payments Over Interchange Fees
summary: eBay has announced it will no longer accept American Express card payments due to "unacceptably high" interchange fees, citing the availability of numerous alternative payment methods for its customers. This decision, while potentially saving eBay money in the short term, has been criticized by analysts like Brian Riley of Javelin Strategy & Research, who believes it could harm eBay in the long run by alienating high-spending Amex customers. American Express expressed disappointment, stating that eBay's move is inconsistent with increasing competition at the point of sale and that eBay accounts for a very small portion of their total network volume.

title: BNPL Company Affirm Launches New Payment Options To Boost Flexibility
summary: Affirm Holdings, Inc. (AFRM) has introduced two new payment options, Pay in 2 and Pay in 30, to enhance payment flexibility and affordability for consumers using its app. These new options allow for interest-free payments divided into two installments or full payment within 30 days without fees, primarily targeting e-commerce transactions under $150. The rollout has already improved cart conversion rates within the app, and Affirm plans to extend these options to its merchant partners soon.

title: BNPL Company Affirm Launches New Payment Options To Boost Flexibility
summary: Affirm Holdings, Inc. (AFRM) has introduced new payment options, Pay in 2 and Pay in 30, to enhance flexibility and affordability for its consumers. These options, allowing for two interest-free payments or payment in full within 30 days, have already improved app conversion rates and are set to expand to merchant partners. Affirm also recently broadened its partnership with Alterra Mountain Company to stimulate travel spending.

title: Topgolf Callaway Brands Joins Forces with Visa
summary: Topgolf Callaway Brands has announced a multiyear strategic agreement with Visa, impacting its brands including Topgolf, Callaway, and TravisMathew. This partnership will offer co-promotional opportunities and benefits for Visa cardholders, particularly Cash App cardholders, such as gameplay offers and early reservation access at Topgolf venues. The collaboration also includes a "Topgolf Block Party Challenge presented by Cash App" with a $50,000 prize and plans for a co-branded credit card in the future.

title: Amex banks on spending at high-end restaurants
summary: American Express is significantly investing in the high-end restaurant sector through its planned acquisition of Tock, a reservation platform, and Rooam, a payments platform. This strategy aims to capitalize on increased consumer spending in restaurants and offer premium experiences to its cardholders. Analysts view this move as a way to bolster Amex's position in a growing industry and expand their merchant acceptance.

title: 21Shares files S-1 for spot Solana ETF in the US
summary: Investment firm 21Shares has filed an S-1 form with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for a Solana-based exchange-traded fund (ETF), following a similar filing by VanEck. This move signals increasing interest in Solana ETFs, with 21Shares believing Solana (SOL) should be treated as a commodity, despite the SEC Enforcement Division's previous declaration of SOL as a security. Legal experts, however, expect significant roadblocks to approval due to the SEC's stance and the absence of a regulated futures market for SOL.

title: Visa-Mastercard settlement failed to treat merchants ‘equitably’
summary: A proposed settlement between Visa, Mastercard, and merchants was rejected by a judge because it failed to treat large and small merchants equitably. The judge, Margo Brodie, determined that larger merchants, who often negotiate lower interchange rates, would not benefit as much as smaller merchants from the proposed rate reductions and surcharging rights. Additionally, the settlement did not address the "honor all cards" rule, which some larger merchants argue contributes to anti-competitive practices.

title: Trends in Truck Transport Refrigeration Units
summary: The trucking industry is transitioning to electric and hybrid Transport Refrigeration Units (TRUs) to meet sustainability goals and regulations, especially in California. This shift involves developing all-electric medium-duty trucks with integrated TRUs, exploring e-axle systems for heavy-duty applications, and overcoming challenges related to charging infrastructure. Telematics and data analysis play a crucial role in managing this transition and optimizing electric TRU deployment.

title: Supreme Court 'swipe fees' ruling may open US regulations to more suits
summary: The U.S. Supreme Court has revived a North Dakota convenience store's challenge to a Federal Reserve regulation on debit card "swipe fees." This 6-3 decision could potentially broaden opportunities for businesses to contest long-standing federal rules. The ruling centered on a 2021 lawsuit filed by Corner Post, which argued it shouldn't be bound by a six-year statute of limitations to challenge the 2011 rule because it started business after the deadline.

title: Legal Fee Tracker: Lawyers' $170 million payday in limbo in credit card swipe fee case
summary: A $170 million legal fee for lawyers who negotiated an antitrust settlement with Visa and Mastercard is now uncertain after a federal judge rejected the proposed deal. The judge found the settlement, intended to limit credit card swipe fees, did not go far enough to benefit merchants despite the substantial legal fees approved. This rejection means attorneys will need to seek further concessions from Visa and Mastercard, likely prolonging the litigation.

title: VIDEO: ETF of the Week: Invesco S&P 500 Quality ETF (SPHQ)
summary: This article highlights the Invesco S&P 500 Quality ETF (SPHQ), discussed by Todd Rosenbluth of VettaFi and Chuck Jaffe of "Money Life." SPHQ focuses on approximately 100 high-quality S&P 500 companies with strong balance sheets and consistent earnings, outperforming the broader S&P 500. The fund is presented as a potential core replacement or complement for investors seeking diversified exposure to top-tier companies.

title: Visa-Mastercard settlement generates thousands of claim conflicts
summary: A federal judge has granted a 90-day extension, until August 30, for U.S. merchants to file claims in the $5.5 billion Visa-Mastercard class-action settlement. This extension was sought due to tens of thousands of conflicting claims filed for the same businesses, often by multiple third-party filers, and to allow more businesses to submit claims for excessive interchange fees paid between 2004 and 2019. Despite a separate, recent settlement being denied preliminary approval, the current claims process remains unaffected, aiming to ensure as many eligible merchants as possible receive their entitled monetary relief.

title: Filings detail owners of The Dakota Scout and Argus Leader
summary: Legal filings have disclosed the ownership of The Dakota Scout and Argus Leader, a requirement for newspapers designated to publish legal notices in South Dakota. The Dakota Scout's ownership, primarily its co-founders Jonathan Ellis and Joe Sneve with 52%, includes several individuals and LLCs, one notable investor being philanthropist Matt Paulson. Meanwhile, the Argus Leader, owned by the publicly traded Gannett, lists 17 financial groups and trust companies as major stakeholders, highlighting a contrast in ownership structures.

title: Judge rejects proposed $30B Visa, Mastercard settlement over merchant fees
summary: A New York judge has rejected a proposed $30 billion settlement between Visa and Mastercard and a class of merchants regarding credit card swipe fees. The settlement aimed to provide equitable relief by slashing merchant fees, but the rejection was supported by The Retail Industry Leaders Association, which deemed the credit card payment market to be broken. The original settlement, reached after seven years of litigation, included rule changes for merchant fees, estimated to be worth nearly $30 billion, and a $15 million education fund for merchants.

title: Visa announces $2.7 billion preferred stock conversion
summary: Visa Inc. announced the conversion of approximately $2.7 billion in Series B and Series C Convertible Participating Preferred Stock into common stock, following a mandatory assessment related to its 2016 acquisition of Visa Europe. This conversion will result in the issuance of about 99,264 shares of Series A Convertible Participating Preferred Stock, effective July 19, 2024, which will automatically convert into Class A Common Stock upon sale. The move stems from a review of potential litigation liabilities concerning interchange fees in the Visa Europe territory.

title: JPMorgan Chase books $7.9 billion gain on sale of Visa stake
summary: JPMorgan Chase announced a $7.9 billion gain from the sale of its Visa Inc. stake, which was included in its second-quarter profit. This move is part of a plan initiated in 2023 allowing big banks to divest portions of their ownership in the credit-card company. JPMorgan had previously stated in May that Visa accepted its tender of 37.2 million shares of Visa Class B-1 common stock in exchange for Visa Class B-2 and Class C common stock, with an $8 billion gain related to the Class C stock being announced at that time.

title: PNC Earnings: Net Interest Income Holds Up Relatively Well
summary: PNC reported second-quarter earnings per share of $3.39, with net interest income performing better than expected, up 1% sequentially. The bank anticipates further benefits from repositioning its balance sheet by replacing low-yielding securities with higher-yield ones. Management projects a positive impact on Net Interest Income in 2025 and expects to decrease core expenses by 1% for the year.

title: JPMorgan Chase invests in B2B payments startup Slope
summary: JPMorgan Chase's payments unit has invested in B2B payments startup Slope, participating in a $65 million financing round that included $15 million in equity and $50 million in debt. Slope, founded in 2021, specializes in AI-powered payments automation for order-to-cash workflows and will join JPMorgan's payments partners network. This investment highlights JPMorgan's strategy to stay updated on payments innovation and leverage Slope's technology to enhance client services.

title: Travelers Stock Was Down 8% In A Day. Why?
summary: Travelers' stock (TRV) dropped 8% on July 19th after its second-quarter revenues and premiums missed street estimates despite year-on-year growth. The company is currently trading at a 9% discount to its fair value of $224, according to Trefis estimates. Despite underperforming the S&P 500 in 2021 and 2023, Travelers saw a 12% year-over-year revenue increase in Q2 2024, driven by growth in premiums and net investment income, with projections for continued revenue growth in FY2024.

title: Capital One customers sue to block $35 billion Discover merger
summary: Two Capital One customers have filed a class-action lawsuit to block the proposed $35 billion merger between Capital One and Discover Financial, claiming it would reduce competition and drive up prices. The lawsuit, filed in Virginia federal court, argues the deal violates U.S. antitrust law and would diminish competitive forces in the credit card market. Capital One has stated the lawsuit "has no merit," while U.S. regulators have not yet taken formal action on the merger.

title: U.S. Bank Launches Accounts Receivables Platform in Partnership with Billtrust
summary: U.S. Bank has launched its new Accounts Receivable platform, U.S. Bank Advanced Receivables, in partnership with Billtrust. This platform aims to help businesses accelerate cash flow, lower costs through automation, and provide better payment experiences by transforming the entire receivables process. The offering integrates U.S. Bank's payment and risk management capabilities with Billtrust's AR technology, featuring solutions for invoicing, payments, cash application, collections, and credit.

title: Visa Hit By Japan's First-Ever Antitrust Action Against Credit Card Industry
summary: Japan's Fair Trade Commission (FTC) has taken its first-ever antitrust action against the credit card industry, targeting Visa Worldwide Pte Ltd., a subsidiary of Visa Inc. The action addresses alleged monopolistic practices where Visa reportedly forced credit card companies to use its proprietary credit authorization system. Visa has agreed to a voluntary corrective action plan to address these concerns.

title: TD Bank Promotes Juan Gorricho as Head of Business Intelligence and Data Transformation
summary: TD Bank has promoted Juan Gorricho to Head of Business Intelligence and Data Transformation for both the US and Canada. Gorricho brings over two decades of experience in leveraging data and analytics to drive business value. His career includes significant roles at Visa, TSYS, and Partners Federal Credit Union, demonstrating extensive expertise in data platforms, governance, and strategy.

title: Visa CEO ‘strongly’ disagrees with class settlement ruling
summary: Visa's CEO, Ryan McInerney, expressed strong disappointment with a federal judge's rejection of a class-action settlement with merchants, calling it unfair despite arguments from merchant lawyers regarding significant savings. He stated that Visa is pursuing a revised settlement, but acknowledges the case could proceed to trial, suggesting a settlement is possible at any stage of the legal process. McInerney also highlighted the complexity of the payments ecosystem, which he believes the judge's decision failed to fully consider.

title: Milberg roils Visa-Mastercard settlement claims process
summary: The law firm Milberg Coleman Bryson Phillips Grossman submitted over 115 fraudulent documents claiming to represent businesses in a $5.5 billion Visa and Mastercard class-action settlement. Milberg blamed a "problematic third-party referral source" for the fake filings involving "high-profile corporations" and has since terminated the relationship, disciplined an employee, and agreed to pay $25,000 to the settlement administrator for costs incurred. The firm also agreed to refer the responsible third party to law enforcement.

title: Reset: How This Public Benefit Corporation Helps Working-Class Americans Improve Financial Health
summary: Reset is a public benefit corporation aiming to improve the financial health of working-class Americans through its Visa card and financial companion app. Founded by Matt Dicou, Wes Rodriguez, and Brian Mascarenhas, the company offers access to earned wages, streamlined budgeting, and spending limits that dynamically update with income and spending data. Reset recently secured $2.3 million in pre-seed funding and differentiates itself through its use of both payroll and bank data, employer portability, and interest-free services.

title: With 88% ownership of the shares, Cummins Inc. (NYSE:CMI) is heavily dominated by institutional owners
summary: Institutional investors own 88% of Cummins Inc. (NYSE:CMI) shares, indicating their significant influence on the company's stock price. The Vanguard Group, BlackRock, Inc., and T. Rowe Price Group, Inc. are among the largest shareholders, collectively controlling 51% of the ownership through the top 19 shareholders. Insiders hold less than 1% of the stock but have been purchasing shares recently.

title: Why the Capital One-Discover Merger Makes Sense
summary: The proposed $35 billion Capital One-Discover merger is analyzed for its competitive implications in consumer banking, credit card issuance, and payment networks. The article argues the merger makes sense as it will not create a "too big to fail" institution in banking, nor significantly increase credit card market concentration, but rather disrupt the payment network duopoly of Visa and Mastercard by boosting Discover's network volume.

title: TD Bank Announces Enhancements to TD Cash Secured Credit Card
summary: TD Bank has announced significant enhancements to its TD Cash Secured Credit Card, aligning its rewards structure with the popular TD Cash Credit Card. Cardholders will now earn 3% cash back on a chosen category, 2% on a second category, and 1% on all other eligible purchases, with the ability to change categories quarterly. This initiative aims to help customers build credit history while maximizing their rewards.

title: 3 Funds to Consider for the Front End of the Yield Curve
summary: This article suggests that fixed income investors looking to avoid rate-risk volatility might consider short-term bonds, specifically focusing on the front end of the yield curve. It highlights three Vanguard ETFs—BSV, VGSH, and VCSH—as options for short-term bond exposure, catering to broad market, Treasury, and corporate bond preferences, respectively. The piece emphasizes the potential benefits of short-term bonds in portfolio construction, especially given uncertain rate cut scenarios.

title: Disney CEO Bob Iger Highlights Company’s 'Unmatched Strength' at D23: The Ultimate Disney Fan Event
summary: Disney CEO Bob Iger kicked off D23: The Ultimate Disney Fan Event by emphasizing the company's "unmatched strength" in creativity, innovation, and storytelling, forged over a century. He highlighted Disney's deep bond with fans, the wide appeal of its brands, and its unique ability to bring stories to life in various forms, including theme parks. Iger expressed gratitude to fans for inviting Disney into their lives and reiterated the company's mission to entertain, thrill, and bring joy.

title: Intercontinental Exchange Stock Gained 22% YTD, What’s Next?
summary: Intercontinental Exchange (NYSE: ICE) stock has gained 22% YTD, outperforming the S&P 500, but is still trading 6% below its estimated fair value of $166. The company recently surpassed Q2 FY2024 street estimates with significant revenue growth in its exchanges and mortgage technology segments, despite increased operating expenses impacting net income. Analysts project ICE's total revenues to reach $11.49 billion in FY2024, leading to a GAAP EPS of $6.04 and a valuation of $166.

title: Visa & Mastercard's Singapore sling & an effective income tax rate of 1.1%
summary: The Commerce Commission is reviewing the high fees charged by Visa and Mastercard in New Zealand, which amount to about $1 billion annually for businesses. These global payment giants operate their New Zealand functions through regional hubs in Singapore, allowing them to report substantial profits there while benefiting from significantly lower effective income tax rates (Mastercard at 1.1%, Visa receiving a credit). The article highlights concerns that New Zealanders are paying too much for card payments and that these companies are not contributing significantly to New Zealand's tax revenue despite their lucrative operations in the country.

title: U.S. Small Caliber Ammunition Market Trends Analysis Report 2024-2030 Featuring FN HERSTAL, Hornady, Nammo, Northrop Grumman, Olin, Remington, Rosoboronexport, Sierra, Visa Outdoor, and Winchester
summary: The U.S. small caliber ammunition market is projected to reach USD 4.8 billion by 2030, growing at a CAGR of 2.3% from 2024. This growth is primarily driven by increasing demand for self-defense, sports shooting, and hunting, as well as rising awareness of personal safety. Key segments include 5.56mm caliber ammunition and centerfire products, with online sales channels also contributing significantly to market expansion.

title: Visa-Mastercard settlement claims deadline postponed
summary: A federal judge has extended the deadline for U.S. merchants to file claims in the $5.5 billion Visa-Mastercard class-action settlement to February 4, 2025. This extension, the second granted this year, aims to ensure more eligible businesses can claim their share, especially after additional data from Visa identified a significant number of class members who did not initially receive claim forms. The settlement resolves a long-running antitrust case concerning excessive interchange fees charged by Visa and Mastercard between January 1, 2004, and January 25, 2019.

title: 6 Companies Hiring Sales Professionals in Colombia
summary: This article highlights six companies currently hiring sales professionals in Colombia, reflecting Latin America's increasing economic importance. Businesses across various sectors, including tech, financial services, and manufacturing, are seeking experienced individuals to expand into new markets. The featured companies include Coupa Software, PayJoy, Motorola Solutions, Visa Inc., TaskUs, and Mondelēz International, detailing their offerings and sales recruitment efforts in the region.

title: Western Asset's co-CIO Leech takes leave of absence amid SEC probe
summary: Ken Leech, co-CIO of Western Asset Management, has taken a leave of absence due to a potential SEC enforcement action regarding a probe into past Treasury derivatives trades. The inquiry focuses on whether some clients were favored in allocating gains and losses. This development has impacted Franklin Resources Inc., Western Asset's parent company, with shares falling significantly.

title: HSBC Targets To Double Wealth Business Assets To $131B In UK: Report
summary: HSBC aims to double its UK wealth management assets to £100 billion (approximately $131 billion) within the next five years, targeting the 'mass affluent' market. The bank plans to leverage its global presence and hire more advisors to achieve this goal, focusing on international connectivity and digital channel enhancements. This strategy is part of a broader banking trend to expand into less interest-rate-sensitive sectors and compete with independent financial advisors.

title: How To Buy VISA (V) Stocks & Shares
summary: This article provides a comprehensive guide on how to buy and sell Visa (V) stocks and shares. It covers essential steps such as opening an account, understanding where Visa is traded, conducting research, deciding on an investment strategy, placing orders, and reviewing performance. The article also touches upon the history of Visa, the risks associated with international investments, and discusses Visa's recent financial performance and dividend payments.

title: Former Visa chairman and CEO Al Kelly joins GM board
summary: Alfred F. Kelly, Jr., former chairman and CEO of Visa Inc., has joined General Motors' board of directors. Kelly, who led Visa through significant global growth, will bring financial, tech, and consumer insights to GM as the company focuses on electric vehicles, autonomous technology, and software services. His appointment expands GM's board to 13 directors, enhancing its diverse expertise.

title: VanEck to Close Ethereum Strategy ETF, Reassessing Crypto Investment Approach
summary: VanEck has announced the closure of its futures-based Ethereum Strategy ETF (EFUT) due to a lack of investor interest, with trading ceasing on September 16 and liquidation anticipated around September 23. This decision highlights a broader trend where investors prefer spot-based crypto ETFs over older futures-based funds, as evidenced by the higher assets under management in VanEck's spot Ethereum ETF (ETHV). Industry experts like Nate Geraci anticipated this shift, noting that spot ETFs would render futures-based options obsolete.

title: $197.5M ATM fees class action settlement
summary: Visa and Mastercard have agreed to a $197.5 million settlement regarding a class action lawsuit claiming they charged unlawful surcharges on ATM transactions. The settlement benefits individuals and entities who paid unreimbursed ATM access fees to JP Morgan, Wells Fargo, Bank of America, or banks within the Visa/Mastercard ATM networks between October 1, 2007, and July 26, 2024. Class members can file a claim by January 22, 2025, to receive a cash payment based on the surcharges paid.

title: Americans to get piece of $197.5 million Visa & Mastercard settlement if they paid ATM fee - you just have to apply
summary: Visa and Mastercard have agreed to a $197.5 million settlement following allegations of unlawful surcharges on ATM transactions. Current and former cardholders who paid unreimbursed ATM access fees between October 1, 2007, and July 26, 2024, to specific banks are eligible to claim a portion of the settlement. Individuals who have not been reimbursed or submitted previous claims have until January 22, 2025, to submit a valid claim form online or via mail.

title: Vanguard Unveils Data from Investor Choice Proxy Voting Pilot
summary: Vanguard has released data from its Investor Choice proxy voting pilot, highlighting individual investor engagement and voting preferences during the 2024 proxy season. The pilot, which empowers individual investors in certain Vanguard funds to choose proxy voting policy options, involved approximately 40,000 participants and showed varied policy selections depending on the fund. Vanguard aims to continue expanding access to the proxy voting process to align investments with investors' personal preferences.

title: Investors Bet on Emerging Market Bonds Amid Fed Rate Cut Expectations
summary: Investors are channeling funds into emerging market bond ETFs, anticipating a Federal Reserve rate cut will boost their returns. Major ETFs like the iShares J.P. Morgan USD Emerging Markets Bond ETF and Vanguard Emerging Markets Government Bond ETF have seen significant inflows. This trend reflects an increasing appetite for higher yields and longer-duration assets found in developing markets as US interest rates are expected to drop.

title: Ankur Crawford: ‘When Software Begins to Write Software, Innovation Is Exponential’
summary: Ankur Crawford, a growth equities investor at Fred Alger Management, discusses the long-term case for AI, emphasizing its role in democratizing compute and driving exponential innovation. She draws parallels to the steam engine and industrial revolution, highlighting AI's potential impact on labor and the economy. Crawford also shares her firm's approach to market volatility and the implications of AI on traditional portfolio construction and equity valuations.

title: Justice Department Sues Visa for Monopolizing Debit Markets
summary: The U.S. Department of Justice has filed an antitrust lawsuit against Visa, accusing the card network of monopolizing debit markets and stifling competition. The complaint alleges that Visa uses exclusionary agreements and incentives to maintain its dominance and extract excessive fees, which are ultimately passed on to consumers and businesses. Visa denies the allegations, stating that the market is competitive and that its services provide value to users.

title: Visa Adds $1.5 Billion to Litigation Escrow Account
summary: Visa has authorized a $1.5 billion deposit into its litigation escrow account, established under its U.S. retrospective responsibility plan. This action follows an antitrust lawsuit filed by the U.S. Department of Justice, accusing Visa of stifling competition in the debit card market. Visa's General Counsel Julie Rottenberg called the lawsuit "meritless" and the company plans to vigorously defend itself.

title: Visa boosts litigation funding ahead of US antitrust fight
summary: Visa has allocated an additional $1.5 billion to its litigation escrow account as it prepares to defend against an antitrust lawsuit from the Justice Department concerning its dominance in the debit card market. The company plans to "vigorously" contest the lawsuit, likely relying on a prior Supreme Court decision in Ohio v. American Express. This funding move primarily impacts Visa's Class B shareholders, which include major financial institutions.

title: Visa hit with merchant class action after US Justice Dept antitrust lawsuit
summary: Visa is facing a new class action lawsuit from U.S. merchants, specifically All Wrapped Up Signs and Graphix, following a major antitrust lawsuit filed by the U.S. Justice Department. The merchants accuse Visa (V.N) of anticompetitive practices, including paying rivals not to develop competing networks and threatening merchants with higher fees for using other transaction processing platforms. The lawsuit alleges Visa unfairly dominates the debit card market and seeks to represent potentially hundreds of thousands of businesses harmed by these practices.

title: Visa monopolizes debit card networks, DOJ lawsuit claims
summary: The U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) has filed an antitrust lawsuit against Visa Inc., alleging the company maintains an unlawful monopoly on debit card networks. The lawsuit claims Visa engages in anticompetitive practices, such as penalizing banks and merchants using alternative payment systems and making agreements with technology companies like Apple, PayPal, and Square to prevent them from becoming competitors. These actions have allowed Visa to control over 60% of debit card transactions and charge more than $7 billion in processing fees, which the DOJ argues are passed on to consumers.

title: Why this money manager is buying American Express and Aon, and selling Comfort Systems
summary: Effie Wolle, president and CIO at GFI Investment Counsel, discusses his long-term investment strategy focusing on companies with growth potential and low obsolescence risk. He highlights recent buys, American Express and Aon, and a recent sale of Comfort Systems USA, explaining the rationale behind each decision based on business models, valuation, and growth prospects.

title: Visa and Mastercard: Top Payment Stocks to Watch After Rate Cuts
summary: This article discusses the investment prospects of Visa (NYSE: V) and Mastercard (NYSE: MA) after the Federal Reserve's recent rate cut. While the rate cut's impact on variable-rate credit cards may be minimal, the consistently high APR margins are beneficial for payment processing companies. The article examines each company's growth potential, noting Visa's strong earnings outlook despite recent antitrust lawsuits, and Mastercard's strategic acquisition of Recorded Future for enhanced cybersecurity and value-added services.

title: VanEck establishes $30 million venture fund to support crypto and AI startups
summary: VanEck has launched a new $30 million venture fund, VanEck Ventures, to invest in early-stage companies in fintech, digital assets, and AI sectors. Led by Wyatt Lonergan and Juan Lopez, the fund targets investments between $500,000 and $1 million for 25-30 projects, with a focus on tokenization, internet-native financial marketplaces, and next-generation payment systems, particularly stablecoin innovations. This initiative aligns with VanEck's strategy to expand its involvement in the digital asset space beyond its existing ETF offerings.

title: Argentina to make available additional spectrum for 5G services
summary: The Argentine government announced it will release additional spectrum for 5G services, totaling 150 megahertz, previously held by state company Arsat and regulator Enacom. title: NY Attorney General launches probe into Capital One’s $35.3bn deal with Discover Financial

title: PayPal Stock Price Forecast - PYPL Shares Poised for Major Comeback as $20B Buyback Drive Value
summary: PayPal Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:PYPL) is trading at $63.04, significantly below its 2021 highs, but analysts predict a major comeback driven by strong Q3 2025 results, a new dividend policy, and a $20 billion share buyback program. The company delivered solid financial performance with $8.42 billion in revenue and $1.97 billion in operating cash flow, along with a strategic pivot towards AI-driven commerce through a partnership with OpenAI. Despite competitive pressures, PayPal's valuation gap, robust capital return program, and focus on profitability make it a compelling value opportunity with a target range of $90-$100 in the next 12 months.

title: MUFG buy-in deal jacks up Gcash valuation to $5B
summary: MUFG Bank Ltd. has completed the acquisition of an 8-percent stake in Ayala-led Mynt, the operator of GCash, boosting its valuation to $5 billion. This transaction follows an initial announcement last August, with the Japanese bank injecting $393 million into the e-wallet brand. Ayala Group’s AC Ventures Holdings Inc. also increased its ownership in GCash by acquiring an additional 8 percent interest for P22.9 billion, bringing its stake to 13 percent.

title: Trio of firms hope to make paying for an EV charge simpler
summary: EFTCorp, Rubicon, Visa, and Verifone have introduced a new open-loop payment system for electric vehicle charging, aiming to simplify the process for EV owners. This solution allows users to pay with a credit card directly at charging stations, eliminating the need for third-party payment accounts. The initiative is expected to increase the accessibility of EV charging and promote greater adoption of electric vehicles in South Africa, with potential for scaling to other regions and services.

title: Payments players mull new approaches to fraud
summary: Companies in the payments industry, including Google, Nacha, Early Warning Services, and Truist, are actively seeking new strategies to combat push-payment fraud, which cost the Americas $102.6 billion in 2023. These organizations are advocating for increased data sharing, greater involvement from law enforcement, and improved digital identity tracking to better protect consumers and corporate customers from sophisticated scam operations. The challenge lies in balancing fraud prevention with maintaining frictionless payment experiences and managing the vast scale of transactions under constant attack from criminal groups.

title: What drove this Vanguard fund to just top the U.S.’s oldest and largest ETF by $1.5 billion
summary: The Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO) has surpassed the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY) in assets under management, becoming the world's largest exchange-traded fund. VOO now holds almost $632 billion, about $1.5 billion more than SPY, which was previously the oldest and largest U.S. ETF. This shift is attributed to VOO's lower cost in tracking the S&P 500 index.

title: How Capital One and Discover Forged US$33.5bn Merger
summary: Capital One and Discover Financial Services shareholders have approved a US$33.5 billion merger, aiming to create a payments and banking powerhouse to challenge Visa and Mastercard. The acquisition leverages Discover's payment network and Capital One's technology prowess, but faces regulatory hurdles and antitrust concerns despite shareholder support. The combined entity would control over US$630 billion in assets and aims for a finalization in early 2025.

title: Worried about U.S. stocks? You can diversify in a market loaded with potential
summary: An investment strategy that has worked for years might eventually make up a large portion of a portfolio, increasing overall risk. The S&P 500 has performed well but has also become concentrated in a small number of stocks. To diversify and mitigate this risk, Shuntaro Takeuchi of Matthews Asia recommends U.S. investors consider adding exposure to the Japanese market.

title: Institutions own 43% of Invesco Mortgage Capital Inc. (NYSE:IVR) shares but individual investors control 57% of the company
summary: Individual investors hold a significant majority of 57% in Invesco Mortgage Capital Inc. (NYSE:IVR), while institutions own 43% of the company's shares. This distribution suggests that individual investors have substantial influence over management decisions. BlackRock, Inc. is the largest institutional shareholder with 9.2% of shares outstanding.

title: Managing Cash With Money Market Funds vs. ETFs
summary: This article examines the growing trend of money market ETFs as an alternative to traditional money market mutual funds for cash management. It highlights key differences, including tradability, floating NAVs, and accessibility, while noting their similar regulatory frameworks and investment goals. The piece also discusses the impact of interest rates and market uncertainty on the appeal of these cash management tools.

title: Ally Financial: Planned Credit Card Business Sale Shows Renewed Focus On Core Business
summary: Ally Financial is selling its credit card business to concentrate on its core operations, primarily car loans, in an effort to recover from past difficulties. This sale is expected to be income-neutral while increasing tangible book value by $1 per share. With a low price/book ratio and a Forward P/E of 10.46, the company shows potential value, especially with planned share repurchases and a renewed focus on profitable segments despite retaining exposure to interest rate and market risks.

title: Amex, Alipay target fast-growing China market
summary: American Express has partnered with Chinese digital payment giant Alipay to expand its presence in China, the world's fastest-growing card market. Amex customers can now add their credit cards to Alipay digital wallets, leveraging Amex's 2020 license to clear local currency transactions in China. This move positions Amex to benefit from the projected 46.8% increase in card use in the Asia-Pacific region by 2029.

title: Mastercard taps State Dept official for top role
summary: Mastercard has announced that its former legal boss, Richard Verma, will rejoin the company as chief administrative officer after serving two years at the State Department. Concurrently, Tim Murphy, the current CAO, has been promoted to vice chairman. Verma's return is notable as Mastercard faces various litigations, including a 20-year dispute over merchant interchange fees and a civil probe by the Justice Department regarding its debit card practices.

title: Condenan al BBVA y a Prisma a pagar una multa por daño punitivo a un cliente a quien no le atendieron su reclamo para desconocer un consumo que no había hecho
summary: The Commercial Chamber's "Sala E" condemned BBVA and Prisma Medios de Pago to pay a fine for punitive damages to a client due to their negligent handling of his claim regarding an unauthorized credit card charge. The companies failed to properly respond to the client's dispute concerning a $543.83 transaction made in Mexico, violating consumer protection laws. This decision reinforces the obligation of financial institutions to adhere to established procedures for credit card disputes and to provide dignified treatment to consumers.

title: Visa CEO Ryan McInerney sells $3.13 million in shares
summary: Visa CEO Ryan McInerney sold 8,620 shares of Visa Class A common stock for approximately $3.13 million, as part of a pre-established trading plan. Concurrently, he exercised stock options to acquire the same number of shares for about $696,668. The transactions occurred while Visa's stock was trading near its 52-week high, and the company maintains a strong financial health score according to InvestingPro.

title: DIA vs. SDY: Which State Street ETF Is the Better Dividend Stock?
summary: This article compares two State Street ETFs, SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) and SPDR S&P Dividend ETF (SDY), for investors seeking dividend income. While DIA offers better growth and overall returns due to its exposure to Dow Jones stocks and even some Magnificent 7 components like Microsoft, SDY provides a higher dividend yield and lower beta, making it suitable for income-oriented investors prioritizing stability. The choice depends on an investor's preference for growth with some income or pure income with stability.

title: Growth & Electronification Could Enhance MBS Opportunities
summary: The U.S. mortgage-backed securities (MBS) market is expanding and becoming more efficient due to electronification, making it a promising area for fixed income investors. Despite past illiquidity issues, new technological advancements are making MBS more accessible, with a significant increase in issuance to $1.1 trillion by Q3 of last year. ETFs like the Vanguard Mortgage-Backed Securities Index Fund ETF Shares (VMBS) offer an all-inclusive and cost-effective option for retail investors to gain exposure to this evolving market.

title: Earnings call transcript: Descartes Systems Q2 2025 revenue hits record high
summary: Descartes Systems Group reported record Q2 2025 revenues of $179.8 million, a 10% increase year-over-year, and record net income of $38 million. The company's adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 44.6%, driven by strong services revenue and strategic acquisitions like PackageRoute and Finale Inventory. Descartes remains debt-free with significant cash reserves and is focusing on AI and technology investments to navigate a complex global trade environment.

title: Visa and Access Bank introduce revolutionary ‘Tap to Phone’ payment solution in Nigeria
summary: Visa, a leader in digital payments, has partnered with Access Bank in Nigeria to launch 'Tap to Phone', an innovative payment solution. This service transforms NFC-enabled Android smartphones into payment terminals, allowing merchants to accept Visa payments by tapping a card to the phone. The initiative aims to enhance financial inclusion, empower small businesses, and drive Nigeria towards a more digital and inclusive financial future, building on Visa’s global efforts to support small and micro-sized businesses.

title: Live Nation Loses Bid to Narrow DOJ Ticketmaster Case
summary: A federal judge in New York denied Live Nation Entertainment Inc.'s attempt to narrow the Justice Department’s antitrust case against it, which seeks to break off Ticketmaster. The DOJ and some 30 states allege Live Nation has illegally monopolized the live events industry, controlling a significant portion of concert venues and ticketing. A trial is scheduled for March 2026.

title: Cartel Crackdown Could Hit Remitly and Western Union
summary: Remittance companies Remitly and Western Union are facing increased scrutiny and risk due to a trifecta of challenges: slowing growth in key markets, growing competition from more affordable payment options like peer-to-peer apps and cryptocurrency, and a federal crackdown on cross-border transfers linked to cartels. The Trump administration has designated cartels as terrorist groups, leading to new FinCEN restrictions and potential legal ramifications for financial institutions processing cartel-linked transactions. This heightened regulatory environment, coupled with existing competition and scrutiny over companies' pricing practices, could significantly impact the profitability and operations of these remittance providers, putting a strain on immigrants sending money home.

title: The Compound and Friends: Big Market Delusion
summary: This article announces a new episode of "The Compound and Friends" podcast, titled "Big Market Delusion." The episode, sponsored by VanEck, discusses topics including TSLA performance, U.S. equity valuations, the S&P 500 selloff, bullish European stocks, and making a case for small caps. The article also promotes the Morningstar Investment Conference.

title: Visa’s chief risk officer Paul Fabara sells $12.9 million in stock
summary: Paul Fabara, Visa's Chief Risk and Client Services Officer, sold 39,350 shares of Visa's Class A common stock for approximately $12.9 million after exercising stock options. Following these transactions, Fabara now directly holds 26,413 shares. The company has also been actively fighting fraud, preventing over $350 million in scam attempts with analyst ratings remaining largely positive.

title: Lawsuit Against Lockheed Martin Criticizes Firm for Using In-House TDFs
summary: A lawsuit has been filed against Lockheed Martin, alleging that the company violated its fiduciary duties by using underperforming, high-fee in-house target-date funds (TDFs) in its 401(k) plans for its own benefit. The plaintiffs claim that Lockheed Martin Investment Management Co. (LMIMCo), Lockheed's subsidiary, offered TDFs that were two to five times more expensive and performed worse than TDFs from independent providers like Vanguard, while also marketing them as the sole investment needed for retirement. The lawsuit seeks a declaration of breach of duties under ERISA and disgorgement of sums derived from the alleged improper transactions.

title: AI will maintain Moody’s market lead, says Stephen Connolly
summary: The article discusses how Moody's, a veteran financial data provider and a long-held Warren Buffett investment, has adapted to modern technology, including AI, to maintain its market leadership. It highlights Moody's strong business model, its resilience against competition due to its "moat," and its continued growth opportunities in the financial services industry, forecasting strong sales and earnings ahead. The author emphasizes that AI will likely strengthen Moody's dominant market position rather than unsettle it, due to the critical need for accurate and authoritative financial data.

title: Galileo Is Tops Among Digital Debit Issuers, Javelin Says
summary: A Javelin Strategy & Research report ranks Galileo Financial Technologies LLC's Digital First product as the leader among digital debit card issuers, citing its flexibility, security, and scalability. The product allows consumers to use a digital card immediately while a physical card with the same details is mailed. Thales and FIS also earned strong recognition as overall leaders in the digital issuance scorecard.

title: Shark Tank’s Anupam Mittal to NPCI: Time to disrupt companies like Visa and MasterCard with UPI
summary: Anupam Mittal, judge on Shark Tank India, advocates for leveraging India's UPI system to challenge global payment giants like Visa and Mastercard, citing its costless transactions. He urges the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) to push UPI's global expansion. Meanwhile, NPCI is working to mitigate fraud by restricting the 'Collect Payments' feature.

title: Company speaks on establishing data center in Nigeria, FG react
summary: Visa Inc. plans to establish a data center infrastructure in Nigeria, reiterating its commitment to the Nigerian market with over $1 billion in investments, including $200 million in Interswitch. Vice President Kashim Shettima praised Visa's investment and assured continued government support, highlighting Nigeria's growing digital economy and fintech landscape. The move aims to introduce new technologies and bolster mobile payment services in the country.

title: Grazzy, U.S. Bank Debit Card Program Simplifies the Way Tipped Employees Earn and Receive Digital Tips
summary: Grazzy and U.S. Bank have partnered to launch a prepaid debit card program designed to simplify digital tip access for hourly employees. This initiative allows employers to issue physical debit cards, enabling employees to receive tips and wages at the end of each shift, even without traditional bank accounts. The program aims to improve financial wellness, offer flexible pay options for employees, and potentially help businesses with employee retention and cost savings.

title: In a world of flux, fundamentals (and active stock-picking) matter.
summary: This article by Justin P. White, CFA, discusses the importance of investing in high-quality, "durable compounder" companies in a world of economic and geopolitical uncertainty. These companies exhibit consistent double-digit earnings growth, pricing power, and sustainable competitive advantages, enabling them to navigate market volatility and generate superior shareholder returns over time. The author highlights examples like Hilton Hotels, Chubb, and Visa as companies possessing these key characteristics.

title: ETFs Around the World: iShares MSCI Emerging Markets ETF (IEM) vs Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets Shares ETF (VGE)
summary: This article compares two prominent Emerging Markets ETFs: the iShares MSCI Emerging Markets ETF (IEM) and the Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets Shares ETF (VGE). It examines their fund objectives, profiles, holdings, performance, distributions, and fees, highlighting that while both offer diversified exposure to emerging markets, they exhibit differences in management fees and historical returns over various timeframes. The analysis aims to help investors navigate these options for potential growth opportunities.

title: OLB Group Announces Support for Mastercard Cryptocurrency Processing
summary: The OLB Group, Inc. has announced its readiness to process Mastercard Bitcoin payments through its OmniSoft business management platform and SecurePay Payment Gateway Platform. This move follows Mastercard's support for cryptocurrency, aiming to accelerate public acceptance of Bitcoin and other digital currencies for everyday transactions. OLB's platforms support multiple cryptocurrencies and offer comprehensive payment options, including conversion to fiat currencies and direct transactions with various crypto wallets.

title: WEX SPARK Health & Benefits 2025 Gathers Industry Leaders to Drive Innovation, Business Growth
summary: WEX is hosting its SPARK Health & Benefits 2025 event in San Diego from March 31 to April 3, bringing together industry leaders to discuss innovation in the health and benefits sector. The event will focus on topics such as AI-driven insights for benefits decisions, simplifying reimbursement processes, enhancing fraud detection, and understanding policy objectives. Key features include the WEX Innovation Experience and the WEX Community Awards, recognizing industry achievements.

title: Matt McGowan Appointed Senior Vice-President, Business Solutions, Bell Media
summary: Bell Media has appointed Matt McGowan as its new Senior Vice-President, Business Solutions. In this role, McGowan, formerly of Snapchat Canada, will lead the advertising sales and partnerships strategy for Canada’s largest media and entertainment company. His extensive experience in media and technology is expected to drive Bell Media's transformation into a digital media and content leader.

title: DJD ETF Holdings List — AMEX:DJD
summary: This article provides a detailed list of the top holdings for the Invesco Dow Jones Industrial Average Dividend ETF (DJD) as of February 26, 2026. It includes the weight percentage, shares, and market value for each company held within the ETF, such as Verizon, Merck, Chevron, and Johnson & Johnson. The information offers insights into the fund's composition and its major investments.

title: Top 10: Women in Fintech
summary: This article highlights the top 10 influential women in the Fintech industry, recognizing their leadership and significant contributions. It profiles executives from major companies like Visa, PayPal, Klarna, Nasdaq, and JPMorgan Chase, detailing their roles in digital transformation, technological innovation, and financial inclusion. The piece emphasizes their impact on shaping the future of finance and technology.

title: XLF ETF Holdings List — AMEX:XLF
summary: This article provides a list of the top holdings for the State Street Financial Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLF) as of February 25, 2026. Key holdings include Berkshire Hathaway Inc. Class B, JPMorgan Chase & Co., and Visa Inc. Class A, detailing their weight percentage, shares, and market value within the ETF.

title: Why I Believe JEPI and JEPQ ETFs Are Still Strong Investments Despite a Weak Stock Market
summary: This article argues that JPMorgan's JEPI and JEPQ ETFs remain strong investment options even in a volatile stock market. These actively managed funds offer high-yield and portfolio diversification by investing in S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 stocks, respectively, and generating income through covered call strategies. While JEPI focuses on blue-chip stocks for steady income, JEPQ is more tech-focused but both aim to provide robust returns despite market downturns.

title: Why Europe is yet to see a non-AAA CLO ETF
summary: Europe has not yet seen a non-AAA CLO ETF due to restrictive regulatory challenges, despite success in the US with products like VanEck's $1bn non-AAA CLO ETF (CLOI). European regulations, particularly from the Central Bank of Ireland, require publicly listed CLO ETFs to maintain at least 80% exposure to AAA-rated tranches, making it difficult to replicate US strategies that include lower-rated securities. This regulatory environment, combined with a perceived saturation in the AAA CLO ETF space, hinders the launch of more diverse CLO ETF offerings in Europe.

title: Visa CEO Ryan McInerney sells $3 million in stock
summary: Visa CEO Ryan McInerney sold 8,620 shares of Class A Common Stock for approximately $3.02 million. This transaction occurred under a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan and near Visa's 52-week high. The article also highlights Visa's strong performance, its bid to replace Mastercard for Apple's credit card, and efforts to integrate with cryptocurrency wallets and combat scams.

title: Affirm director Keith Rabois sells $730,520 in stock
summary: Keith Rabois, a director at Affirm Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ: AFRM), recently sold 16,088 shares of company stock for approximately $730,520. Following this transaction, conducted under a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan, Rabois retains 45,432 shares. The sale occurred as Affirm's stock has declined year-to-date, despite recent positive news regarding a partnership with Stride Bank and continued optimistic analyst ratings.

title: Consumers Plan to Use Tax Refunds To Pay Down Debt, ACI Finds
summary: A survey by ACI Worldwide Inc. reveals that 39% of consumers plan to use their 2025 tax refunds to pay down credit card debt and other loans, indicating a continued focus on financial stability amidst inflation. The survey, conducted with YouGov Plc, also highlights that 44% intend to deposit refunds into savings, and a growing number of respondents prefer digital payment methods for taxes, though awareness of tax-related scams remains low.

title: VOO, SPY, IVV Shed Assets as Market Rout Continues
summary: The three largest S&P 500 ETFs—VOO, SPY, and IVV—have collectively shed billions in assets, dropping about 7% since a recent market rout began. This decline occurred despite significant inflows from investors "buying the dip," betting on a market turnaround following an initial market slump after President Trump's inauguration and subsequent tariffs. The asset managers have seen their total AUM fall from over $1.7 trillion last week to $1.6 trillion as of Wednesday, with VOO and SPY still attracting billions in new money while IVV experienced outflows.

title: Goldman Sachs Earnings: Strong Start to 2025 as Uncertainty Breeds Heightened Trading Activity
summary: Goldman Sachs Group reported a strong start to the year, driven by exceptional trading revenue due to market volatility, which offset a tepid dealmaking environment. Despite strong quarterly results, shares remain modestly overvalued, and Morningstar maintains a fair value estimate of $490 per share. The global banking and markets segment saw significant net revenue gains, while the asset and wealth management segment experienced mixed results but continued positive net inflows.

title: Europe Real-Time Payments Market Size, & Growth Report, 2033
summary: The Europe real-time payments market, valued at USD 6.52 billion in 2024, is projected to reach USD 17.45 billion by 2033, growing annually at 11.56%. This growth is driven by increasing demand for instantaneous transactions and regulatory support, despite challenges like high implementation costs and cybersecurity risks. Key market opportunities include expanding cross-border payments and integrating emerging technologies like AI and blockchain.

title: Investing in JPMorgan Equity Premium Income ETF (JEPI): A High-Yield Income Opportunity
summary: The article discusses the JPMorgan Equity Premium Income ETF (JEPI) as a high-yield income opportunity for investors. It highlights JEPI's covered-call strategy, diversified portfolio, and strong performance during market volatility, noting its current 8% forward dividend yield. While acknowledging JEPI's tax inefficiency compared to some alternatives, the article concludes that its consistent dividends and downside protection make it an attractive option for income-focused investors, especially given current market conditions.

title: Better Dividend Growth Stock: Costco vs. Visa
summary: This article analyzes Costco (COST) and Visa (V) as dividend growth stocks, highlighting their robust business models and commitment to shareholder returns. While both offer double-digit dividend growth, Visa is presented as the more compelling option due to its higher historical growth rate, lower payout ratio, and asset-light business model. However, the author suggests that including both in a diversified portfolio could be ideal for many dividend growth investors.

title: With The Final OKs, the Capital One-Discover Combo Sets a May 18 Closing
summary: Capital One Financial Corp.'s $35-billion acquisition of Discover Financial Services received its final federal regulatory approvals from the Federal Reserve and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency, clearing the way for a May 18 closing. The merger, announced in February 2024, aims to increase competition in banking and payments, create a more powerful rival to Visa and Mastercard, and leverage Discover's network and credit card portfolio. However, integrating the two companies will present challenges due to their differing corporate cultures and business operations, such as customer service centers.

title: Europe Smart Card Market Size, Share,Trends & Analysis, 2033
summary: The Europe smart card market was valued at USD 3.08 billion in 2024 and is projected to reach USD 4.15 billion by 2033, growing at a CAGR of 3.35% from 2025 to 2033. Key drivers include rising demand for contactless payment solutions and government initiatives for secure identity verification, with Germany dominating the market and Spain showing the fastest growth. Challenges such as high implementation costs, cybersecurity concerns, and interoperability issues need to be addressed for continued expansion.

title: Watch Launch of New Elm Market Navigator ETF | Bloomberg ETF IQ 04/21/2025
summary: This Bloomberg ETF IQ segment discusses current market volatility, ETF flows, and asset allocation strategies, featuring Victor Haghani, CIO of Elm Wealth, and Rebecca Venter, Fixed Income Product Manager at Vanguard. Haghani introduces the new Elm Market Navigator ETF, emphasizing its tax efficiency and dynamic asset allocation approach, while Venter highlights Vanguard's active short-duration bond ETF and its role in managing portfolio duration. The discussion also touches on the concept of "safe haven" assets amidst market uncertainty and the increasing trend of fixed income ETF launches.

title: La audaz estrategia de los bancos para competir con la digitalización y las fintech
summary: Banks are reinventing themselves to compete with fintechs by developing new digital payment solutions. Banco Galicia's Nave, a payment solution initially offering QR codes for account-to-account payments, has evolved to include card payments and integrated e-commerce solutions, demonstrating how traditional financial institutions are adapting. This strategy focuses on providing comprehensive financial platforms, competitive commissions, and personalized services, especially for SMEs, and emphasizes the increasing shift towards secure digital payments over traditional methods.

title: Visa (V) Announces New $30 Billion Share Buyback Program | V Sto
summary: Visa (V) has announced a new $30 billion share buyback program, approved by its board of directors, following a previous repurchase of $4.5 billion in Q1. The company also declared a quarterly cash dividend of 59 cents per share. Wall Street analysts maintain an "Outperform" rating for Visa, with an average target price suggesting a 10.40% upside from its current price.

title: Visa Q2 2025 slides: revenue up 9%, announces $30B share repurchase program
summary: Visa reported strong fiscal Q2 2025 financial results, with net revenue increasing 9% year-over-year to $9.6 billion and non-GAAP EPS up 10% to $2.76. The company also announced a new $30 billion share repurchase program, signaling confidence in its future. Visa's key business drivers, including payments volume and cross-border volume, showed healthy growth, and the company provided an optimistic outlook for the remainder of fiscal year 2025.

title: Shift4 Payments Q1 Earnings: Capitalizing On Payment Tech Growth (NYSE:FOUR)
summary: Shift4 Payments is positioned for substantial growth within the rapidly evolving payments industry, fueled by recent leadership changes and robust earnings, including a 35% year-over-year increase in Q1 payment volume. The company expects 20% organic revenue growth in 2025, driven by innovations like SkyTab, and will expand globally through the $2.5 billion acquisition of Global Blue. Despite competition, Shift4, with a $5 billion market cap, is projected to double in value over five years through both organic and inorganic growth.

title: Analysts Offer Insights on Financial Companies: OneMain Holdings (OMF) and Visa (V)
summary: Analysts have issued bullish sentiments on financial companies OneMain Holdings (OMF) and Visa (V). John Rowan of Janney Montgomery maintained a Buy rating on OneMain Holdings with a $63.00 price target, while Trevor Williams from Jefferies maintained a Buy rating on Visa with a $400.00 price target. Both companies received "Buy" or "Strong Buy" consensus ratings from analysts.

title: Why the Capital One/Discover Deal Is About Much More Than Payments
summary: The Capital One and Discover deal, recently approved by regulators, is poised to reshape not just the payments landscape but also the broader banking industry. Experts anticipate significant impacts on deposit generation, small business finance, and even a potential bid for the Apple Card portfolio. The integration of Discover's debit network, exempt from Durbin amendment restrictions, is seen as a key asset that could significantly boost Capital One's national digital banking strategy and competitive edge.

title: Sam Altman’s World Officially Launches in the U.S., Inks Partnerships with Visa, Stripe, and Match Group
summary: Sam Altman's company, Tools for Humanity, officially launched World in the U.S. with the goal of creating a "human-first identity and financial network" that verifies users as human online, especially in an age of pervasive AI. The service, which provides 16 Worldcoin (WLD) to new users in exchange for an iris scan, has secured partnerships with Visa, Stripe, and Match Group for various financial and verification services. Despite regulatory hurdles and privacy concerns, the company is focusing on expanding its network and plans to monetize through app charges, transaction fees, and mini-apps within the World platform.

title: Green Dot, Crypto.com partner for banking services
summary: Green Dot has partnered with Crypto.com to offer banking services, allowing Crypto.com customers to convert digital assets to fiat currency and access funds at Green Dot locations nationwide. This collaboration, leveraging Green Dot’s embedded finance platform Arc, also introduces an interest-earning savings account for Crypto.com users. The move further integrates Crypto.com with traditional finance, following previous partnerships with Visa and FIS.

title: Two JPMorgan ETFs that are providing a destination for risk-averse investors
summary: JPMorgan's Equity Premium Income ETF (JEPI) and Ultra-Short Income ETF (JPST) are attracting risk-averse investors by offering downside protection and income generation. JEPI aims to provide income by selling out-of-the-money options, while JPST focuses on fixed income to provide portfolio stability. These ETFs are highlighted as popular choices for investors seeking to weather market volatility.

title: Visa Q2 Earnings Top Forecasts, Adds $30B Buyback Plan
summary: Visa (NYSE: V) reported strong fiscal second-quarter 2025 earnings, surpassing analyst expectations with a 9.3% year-over-year increase in net revenue and a 10% rise in non-GAAP EPS. The company's Board of Directors also authorized a new $30 billion multi-year share repurchase program, demonstrating a significant commitment to returning capital to shareholders. These results, coupled with resilient transaction volumes and strategic investments in AI and digital payments, reinforce Visa's strong financial health and market leadership.

title: The 3 Best Warren Buffett Stocks to Buy With $3,000 Right Now
summary: This article identifies three top Warren Buffett-backed stocks—BYD, Visa, and Berkshire Hathaway—as compelling investment opportunities. It suggests that investors with $3,000 could diversify by investing $1,000 into each of these companies. The author highlights BYD's growth in electric vehicles, Visa's dominant payment processing business, and Berkshire Hathaway's diverse holdings and strong balance sheet as reasons for their appeal.

title: Should You Invest in the Fidelity MSCI Financials Index ETF (FNCL)?
summary: The Fidelity MSCI Financials Index ETF (FNCL), launched in 2013, is a passively managed ETF designed for broad exposure to the Financials - Broad segment of the equity market, ranked 3rd within the Zacks sectors. With $2.16 billion in assets and a low expense ratio of 0.08%, it seeks to match the performance of the MSCI USA IMI Financials Index. The ETF has performed well year-to-date and over the last 12 months, holding a Zacks ETF Rank of 2 (Buy).

title: As Stocks Swooned, Individuals Bought & Pros Bailed
summary: During extreme market volatility in April 2025, individual investors bought stocks on the dip, while hedge funds and professional investors sold off shares. This behavior contrasts with past market downturns, largely because individual investors use passively managed index funds in 401(k)s. While hedge funds are forced to sell due to leverage and performance pressures, retail investors who held steady have seen their portfolios recover.

title: Global Payments And FIS Celebrate Their Worldpay-TSYS Deal
summary: Global Payments and FIS are celebrating their Worldpay-TSYS deal, which involves Global Payments acquiring Worldpay for $22.7 billion and FIS acquiring Global's issuing business (TSYS) for $13.5 billion. Global Payments is enthusiastic about Worldpay complementing its merchant business and enhancing its growth profile, while FIS believes the acquisition of TSYS will strengthen its focus on card issuing. Both companies reported their first-quarter financial results, with the deal dominating discussions during their respective analyst calls.

title: Webull Eliminates Fund Transfer Delays: New Visa Partnership Enables Sub-Minute Trading Account Access
summary: Webull has partnered with Visa to integrate Visa Direct into its U.S. platform, allowing real-time money transfers between Webull brokerage accounts and external bank accounts. This collaboration introduces a "Deposit" feature that enables users to access funds in under a minute, significantly reducing the multi-day delays associated with traditional ACH transfers. The initiative aims to enhance market access, investment opportunities, and overall user experience by offering greater speed, flexibility, and security in managing investment funds.

title: Stan Wong's Top Picks: iShares Core MSCI EAFE ETF, MercadoLibre & Visa
summary: Stan Wong, a portfolio manager at Scotia Wealth Management, has shared his top investment picks, which include the iShares Core MSCI EAFE ETF, MercadoLibre, and Visa.
